title: Mechanisms and Circumvention of CD19 Escape after CAR T-Cell Therapy in Pediatric B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cells induce morphologic complete remission in 80 to 90 percent of children and young adults with relapsed or refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, yet 30 to 50 percent relapse within 12 months, and roughly half of those relapses occur with loss of the targeted surface protein. Distinct routes to escape have been described: alternatively spliced CD19 transcripts lacking exon 2, frameshift and missense mutations in exons 2 through 5, defective CD81 chaperone function, lineage switch to a myeloid immunophenotype, and trogocytic transfer of the target from the blast onto the effector cell. This proposal will define the frequency and clonal architecture of each route across 120 paired pre-infusion and relapse specimens, test whether escape variants pre-exist below the limit of routine detection, and translate a bivalent CD19/CD22 receptor into a phase 1 study designed to close the escape window.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Determine the genomic and transcriptomic basis of target-negative relapse. We will apply hybrid-capture deep sequencing of CD19, CD22, and CD81, long-read isoform sequencing, and single-cell RNA sequencing with surface protein capture to 120 paired specimens banked at infusion and at relapse. Error-corrected amplicon sequencing will test whether escape variants are detectable at a fraction of 10^-4 before infusion. Aim 2. Test trogocytosis as a reversible route to reduced surface target density. Primary blasts will be co-cultured with tisagenlecleucel-like products, and receptor-dependent membrane transfer will be quantified by imaging cytometry, together with its effect on fratricide and effector hypofunction. Aim 3. Evaluate a bivalent CD19/CD22 receptor in a phase 1 dose-escalation study (NCT03919240) enrolling 36 subjects, using serial 10-color marrow immunophenotyping at a sensitivity of 0.01 percent to define depth and durability of remission.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Target-negative relapse is now the dominant mode of failure after cellular therapy in pediatric B-ALL and carries a median overall survival under 9 months. Salvage is constrained because blinatumomab engages the same surface protein and because reinfusion of the same product rarely re-induces remission when the target is absent. The field lacks a quantitative map of which escape routes dominate, whether they are selected from pre-existing subclones or acquired under pressure, and which can be pre-empted by receptor design. Resolving this would change post-infusion surveillance, identify which children should proceed to consolidative allogeneic transplant, and supply the mechanistic rationale for dual-targeting constructs now entering early testing. Our paired specimen resource, assembled across four pediatric centers since 2013 under a single collection protocol, is uniquely positioned to deliver these answers within the project period.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Three elements are new. First, long-read isoform sequencing of relapse specimens resolves splice products that short-read data cannot phase, allowing exon 2 skipping to be distinguished from intron retention and from partial exon deletion. Second, our error-corrected amplicon assay reaches a variant allele fraction of 0.05 percent in bulk marrow, enabling a direct test of the pre-existing subclone hypothesis rather than inference from the relapse specimen alone. Third, the bivalent receptor uses a loop configuration with a single 4-1BB endodomain rather than two independently expressed receptors, avoiding the vector packaging limits and unbalanced surface expression that constrained earlier dual-targeting attempts. Mechanism and intervention are therefore tested in the same prospectively enrolled cohort rather than in separate populations.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Specimens comprise 120 paired pre-infusion and relapse marrow aspirates plus 40 non-relapsing controls collected under a common protocol. Sequencing includes hybrid capture across 45 B-lineage genes at 1000x mean depth, Nanopore complementary DNA sequencing for isoform calling, and 10x Genomics 5-prime libraries for 30 index cases. Functional studies co-culture primary blasts with second-generation receptor-modified T cells at effector-to-target ratios of 1:1 through 1:10, quantifying membrane transfer by imaging cytometry. In vivo, NSG mice engrafted with primary patient blasts receive 2e6 receptor-modified cells and are followed by bioluminescence for 60 days, with escape variants recovered at progression. Escape route frequencies will be compared by exact tests with Benjamini-Hochberg control at q less than 0.05; 84 evaluable pairs give 80 percent power to detect a 20 percentage point difference.

title: Single-Cell Determinants of Durable Response and Exhaustion after Axicabtagene Ciloleucel in Large B-Cell Lymphoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Axicabtagene ciloleucel produces durable remission in fewer than half of patients with relapsed large B-cell lymphoma, and much of that split appears to be encoded in the CD19-directed infusion product rather than in the tumor. We propose a single-cell census of 200 infusion products with matched serial post-infusion blood, combining 5-prime transcriptome capture, surface protein tagging, and paired T-cell receptor sequencing. Preliminary data from 42 products show that a CD8-positive population expressing TCF7, IL7R, and SELL is enriched threefold in patients free of progression at 12 months, whereas products dominated by cells co-expressing TOX, ENTPD1, and HAVCR2 fail within 90 days. We will define the trajectory connecting these states after infusion, test whether the dysfunctional program is imposed during manufacture or acquired in vivo, and determine whether transposase-accessible chromatin profiling marks a point of fixed commitment.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Build a single-cell atlas of 200 axicabtagene ciloleucel infusion products with paired receptor sequencing, and relate memory-stem and exhausted compositional fractions to progression-free survival at 12 months. Aim 2. Track clonal fate in vivo. Using shared T-cell receptor clonotypes as barcodes, we will follow individual product clones into day 7, day 14, day 28, and month 3 samples, asking whether expanding clones arise from the memory-stem fraction and whether contraction coincides with acquisition of TOX and coinhibitory receptor expression. Aim 3. Determine whether the dysfunctional state is reversible. Transposase-accessible chromatin profiling of sorted subsets at each timepoint will identify regions that lose accessibility irreversibly, and we will test whether transient inhibition of BATF3 or overexpression of TCF7 during manufacture restores expansion in mice bearing NALM-6 and Raji tumors.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Response to CD19-directed cellular therapy in aggressive lymphoma is bimodal: patients either enter a plateau after 12 months or progress within the first 3. Current clinical variables such as lactate dehydrogenase, tumor bulk, and international prognostic index explain only a modest fraction of that variance, and post-infusion peak expansion is known only after the therapeutic decision has been made. If the composition of the product itself carries most of the information, then release testing could be extended beyond viability and vector copy number to include a functional composition readout, and patients likely to fail could be routed to alternative bridging or to consolidative strategies before infusion. The proposed atlas will also supply the reference against which next-generation manufacturing processes, including shortened culture and interleukin 7 and 15 support, can be judged.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Prior product-composition studies used bulk phenotyping of a handful of markers and could not connect a product subset to the fate of its descendants in the patient. Our design uses the endogenous receptor repertoire as a natural lineage barcode, so that clones can be tracked across five timepoints without engineering an additional tag. We further couple transcriptome and chromatin readouts on the same sorted populations, which allows us to separate a transient activation state from a fixed commitment. Finally, all products come from a single apheresis and manufacturing platform with harmonized release criteria, eliminating the process heterogeneity that has confounded earlier multicenter comparisons of infusion product quality.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Products are sampled at release under an approved amendment; 200 subjects will be accrued over 4 years with 12-month follow-up. Libraries are prepared with 10x Genomics 5-prime chemistry, 137 oligonucleotide-conjugated antibodies, and paired alpha and beta chain enrichment, targeting 8000 cells per sample. Compositional fractions will be modeled with a Dirichlet-multinomial regression against progression-free survival, adjusting for tumor bulk and bridging therapy; 200 subjects give 85 percent power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.55 per interquartile increase in the memory-stem fraction. Clonal tracking will use exact clonotype matching with a shared-clone permutation null. Chromatin libraries will be prepared from 50000 sorted cells with Omni protocols, and differential accessibility will be assessed with a negative binomial model at a false discovery rate of 5 percent.

title: Resistance to and Optimal Sequencing of BCMA- and GPRC5D-Directed Bispecific Antibodies in Relapsed Myeloma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Bispecific antibodies redirecting T cells against BCMA, including teclistamab and elranatamab, produce overall response rates near 60 percent in triple-class exposed multiple myeloma, but most responses are lost within 18 to 24 months. Resistance is heterogeneous: biallelic deletion or truncating mutation of TNFRSF17, gamma-secretase mediated shedding that raises soluble receptor and blocks binding, expansion of CD8 T cells co-expressing PD-1, TIGIT, and CD38 with reduced polyfunctionality, and an immunosuppressive marrow niche rich in myeloid-derived suppressor cells. We will profile 180 patients longitudinally at baseline, best response, and progression, define which resistance class dominates, and test whether switching to the GPRC5D-directed agent talquetamab restores control when the first target is lost. Depth of response will be tracked by sequencing-based clonotype quantification of the dominant immunoglobulin rearrangement at a sensitivity of 10^-6.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Define the landscape of target-side resistance. Whole-exome and targeted sequencing of sorted plasma cells at progression will quantify TNFRSF17 copy loss, truncating variants, and GPRC5D promoter methylation, and paired serum will be assayed for shed receptor. Aim 2. Define effector-side resistance. Mass cytometry and single-cell profiling of marrow T cells at three timepoints will test whether the frequency of CD8 cells co-expressing three or more coinhibitory receptors at baseline is associated with duration of response. Aim 3. Test sequencing strategy prospectively. A 90-patient study (NCT05243342) will randomize patients progressing on BCMA-directed therapy to talquetamab versus investigator choice, with residual disease at 10^-6 as the primary endpoint and with infection density and immunoglobulin replacement recorded as prespecified safety outcomes.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: T-cell redirecting antibodies have moved rapidly into earlier lines of myeloma therapy, yet the field has no framework for choosing the second agent after the first fails. If loss of the first target dominates, switching targets should be effective and switching mechanism unnecessary. If effector dysfunction dominates, target switching will fail and the correct move is a drug holiday, immune modulation, or cellular therapy. These are opposite clinical recommendations and are currently made by intuition. A resistance taxonomy tied to a prospective randomized comparison would immediately inform sequencing decisions for tens of thousands of patients per year and would define which patients should be enrolled on trials of combination approaches rather than serial monotherapy.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Most resistance reports in this disease are single-institution case series with fewer than 20 progression specimens and no matched baseline. We will assemble the first prospectively banked longitudinal resource with sorted plasma cells and marrow T cells at three fixed timepoints in 180 patients, permitting resistance class to be assigned per patient rather than per cohort. We introduce a quantitative shed-receptor assay calibrated against a recombinant standard, which converts a qualitative observation into a continuous covariate. Finally, the embedded randomized comparison converts an observational taxonomy into an actionable rule, with a prespecified interaction test between resistance class assigned at progression and benefit from target switching.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Enrollment: 180 patients receiving BCMA-directed bispecific therapy at four centers, with marrow at baseline, at best response, and at progression. Plasma cells will be sorted to more than 95 percent purity by CD138 selection followed by cell sorting; T cells will be profiled with a 42-marker mass cytometry panel and 5-prime single-cell libraries in 60 index cases. Shed receptor will be measured by electrochemiluminescence with a lower limit of quantification of 0.8 nanograms per milliliter. The randomized substudy uses a 1:1 allocation, 90 patients, and 80 percent power to detect an absolute 25 percentage point difference in the rate of undetectable disease at 10^-6 using a two-sided alpha of 0.05. Time-to-event analyses use cause-specific hazards with death as a competing risk.

title: Myeloid Drivers and Prophylactic Interruption of Neurotoxicity after CD19 CAR T-Cell Therapy

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome affects 30 to 60 percent of patients treated with CD28-containing CD19-directed products and remains the principal driver of intensive care utilization after infusion. Unlike cytokine release syndrome, neurotoxicity responds poorly to interleukin 6 receptor blockade with tocilizumab, implying a distinct upstream driver. We propose that monocyte and macrophage-derived interleukin 1 beta, together with endothelial activation marked by a rising angiopoietin 2 to angiopoietin 1 ratio, initiates blood-brain barrier failure independently of the interleukin 6 axis. We will profile 240 patients with serial cytokine, endothelial, and cerebrospinal fluid sampling, define a pre-infusion risk score, and test prophylactic interleukin 1 receptor antagonism in a phase 2 study. The goal is a mechanism-anchored prevention strategy rather than reactive escalation to high-dose corticosteroids after symptoms appear.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Define the temporal ordering of monocyte activation, endothelial injury, and neurologic signs. Serial blood at 12-hour intervals through day 7 and cerebrospinal fluid at day 3 and at symptom onset will be assayed for 92 analytes, and mediation analysis will test whether interleukin 1 beta precedes and explains the angiopoietin shift. Aim 2. Build and validate a pre-infusion risk score from tumor bulk, platelet count, ferritin, and the frequency of classical monocytes, with derivation in 160 patients and internal validation in 80. Aim 3. Test prophylactic anakinra at 200 milligrams daily from day 0 through day 10 in a single-arm phase 2 study (NCT04150913) of 60 patients, with grade 3 or higher neurotoxicity by ASTCT criteria as the primary endpoint against a historical rate of 28 percent.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Severe neurologic toxicity after infusion drives median intensive care stays of 5 days, delays discharge, restricts delivery to high-resource centers, and is the reason many older patients are never referred. Current management escalates corticosteroids after symptoms appear, an approach that shortens events but may blunt effector expansion and has been associated with inferior progression-free survival in several series. Prevention anchored to the initiating pathway would break that tradeoff. Because interleukin 1 receptor antagonism does not impair effector function in preclinical models while abrogating both toxicity syndromes, a positive prophylaxis result would change standard supportive care and would make outpatient administration feasible for a much larger fraction of patients.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: The proposal moves from association to ordering. Twelve-hour sampling density through the first week, rather than daily sampling, is sufficient to resolve whether the monocyte signal precedes endothelial injury, and paired cerebrospinal fluid allows compartment-specific inference that blood alone cannot support. We add a quantitative endothelial readout, the angiopoietin ratio, that is measurable before infusion and is not simply a downstream inflammatory marker. The phase 2 design uses a prespecified futility boundary at 20 patients and embeds the mechanistic sampling schedule within the interventional cohort, so that pathway engagement can be verified in the same patients in whom clinical benefit is measured.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Two hundred forty adults receiving commercial CD19-directed products for aggressive lymphoma will be enrolled at three centers. Cytokines will be measured on a validated multiplex platform with intra-assay coefficients of variation under 12 percent; classical, intermediate, and nonclassical monocyte fractions will be quantified from cryopreserved cells. Mediation analysis will use inverse-probability weighting with bootstrap confidence intervals. The risk score will be fitted by penalized logistic regression with elastic net regularization and reported with optimism-corrected discrimination. For the interventional aim, a Simon two-stage design with 60 patients provides 90 percent power to detect a reduction in severe neurotoxicity from 28 percent to 12 percent, and correlative sampling will confirm suppression of downstream interleukin 6 and ferritin trajectories.

title: An Allogeneic Gene-Edited CAR T-Cell Platform with Engineered Evasion of Host Immunity

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Autologous manufacture imposes a 3 to 5 week vein-to-vein interval, fails outright in 5 to 10 percent of heavily pretreated patients, and cannot serve patients who progress quickly. A banked, donor-derived CD19-directed product would remove those constraints but faces two immunologic obstacles: donor T cells attacking host tissue, and host T and natural killer cells clearing the graft before it can expand. We will use CRISPR-Cas9 to disrupt TRAC and B2M in a single electroporation, then knock in a non-classical HLA-E single-chain trimer at the B2M locus to restrain natural killer clearance. The program will define the persistence achievable with each configuration in humanized mice, quantify the residual risk of translocation and insertional events by unbiased off-target capture, and support an investigational new drug application in year 4.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Optimize multiplex editing. We will compare simultaneous versus staged disruption of TRAC and B2M for editing efficiency, translocation frequency by droplet digital PCR, and product yield, targeting less than 0.5 percent residual receptor-positive cells after magnetic depletion. Aim 2. Extend graft survival. HLA-E trimer knock-in at the B2M locus will be tested against unedited and B2M-null controls for resistance to purified natural killer cells across 12 donors, and for expansion in mice reconstituted with mismatched human immune systems. Aim 3. Establish a safety package. Unbiased genome-wide off-target capture, integration site mapping of the transgene, and 6-month tumor watch studies in immunodeficient mice will characterize the risk of clonal outgrowth arising from vector integration near proto-oncogenes.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Roughly one in five patients referred for cellular therapy never receives it, most often because disease progresses during manufacture or apheresis yields an inadequate product. Availability on demand would change that arithmetic and would additionally allow redosing, which is impractical when each dose requires a new collection. The barriers are immunologic rather than manufacturing: without receptor disruption, donor cells cause severe host tissue injury, and without evasion engineering, grafts are cleared within 2 to 3 weeks, well before maximal antitumor activity. Solving both in a single product would make on-demand redosing feasible and would provide a platform on which future receptor designs can be tested without re-optimizing the cell source.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Knock-in of an HLA-E trimer at the disrupted B2M locus couples the evasion cassette to the very edit that creates vulnerability, so that every cell lacking surface class I also displays the inhibitory ligand, avoiding the mixed populations produced by random integration. We further apply a translocation-aware quality metric rather than reporting only per-locus editing efficiency, because multiplex cutting generates reciprocal fusions that per-locus assays cannot see. Long-term tumor watch studies with integration site recovery are built in from the outset rather than added after a clinical signal, providing a prospective baseline for judging any future report of a donor-derived clonal proliferation.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Healthy donor apheresis products from 12 donors will be activated, electroporated with ribonucleoprotein complexes, and transduced with a lentiviral vector encoding a 4-1BB-containing CD19-directed receptor. Editing will be quantified by amplicon sequencing and flow-based depletion validation. Translocations between the two cut sites will be measured by droplet digital PCR with a limit of detection of 0.01 percent. In vivo, NSG mice bearing Raji tumors will receive 5e6 cells with weekly bioluminescence; humanized mice reconstituted with mismatched CD34-positive cells will be used for rejection studies with 10 animals per arm. Off-target discovery will use an unbiased double-strand break capture method followed by targeted verification of the top 40 candidate sites at 5000x depth.

title: Harmonizing Flow Cytometric and Sequencing-Based Residual Disease Endpoints across B-Cell Malignancies

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Measurable residual disease is now used to guide consolidation in acute lymphoblastic leukemia and to define depth of response in multiple myeloma, yet the two dominant assays differ in analytic floor, sample requirements, and failure modes. Multiparameter flow cytometry reports a phenotypic estimate on fresh cells within hours; immunoglobulin clonotype sequencing reports a genomic estimate on stored material but requires an informative index specimen. Discordant results are common near 10^-5 and are resolved differently at different centers. This program will run both assays on 900 paired specimens across three diseases, model the sources of discordance, establish conversion rules between platforms, and evaluate whether a negative result at a defined threshold behaves as a valid surrogate for event-free survival at the trial level.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Quantify assay concordance. Paired marrow aspirates from 500 patients with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, 300 with multiple myeloma, and 100 with mantle cell lymphoma will be assayed by an 10-color standardized flow panel and by immunoglobulin sequencing, with hemodilution assessed by mast cell and erythroid precursor content. Aim 2. Model discordance. Bayesian latent class models without a gold standard will estimate assay-specific sensitivity and specificity as a function of burden, sample cellularity, and prior therapy, including patients treated with CD19- and BCMA-directed agents in whom target antigen loss can confound phenotypic gating. Aim 3. Evaluate surrogacy. Using individual patient data from 14 randomized trials, we will estimate trial-level association between treatment effects on undetectable disease and on event-free survival, reporting R-squared with 95 percent confidence intervals.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Regulatory acceptance of a response depth endpoint depends on assay comparability across trials, and comparability is currently assumed rather than demonstrated. When two assays disagree, therapy is intensified in one center and de-escalated in another for the same biology. Establishing calibrated conversion rules would let historical trials be pooled, would allow assays to be used interchangeably within a single protocol, and would clarify which threshold should trigger transplant referral. Because both assays are already deployed at scale, the deliverable is immediately actionable: a published conversion function, a hemodilution correction, and a statement of the burden range in which the two platforms cannot be treated as equivalent.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Prior concordance studies compared assays as if one were truth, which biases the estimated performance of both. Latent class modeling removes that assumption and yields honest sensitivity estimates near the analytic floor, where clinical decisions are actually made. We add a quantitative hemodilution correction derived from non-hematopoietic reference populations, which explains a large share of false-negative phenotypic results in second and third aspirate pulls. Finally, we treat post-immunotherapy specimens as a distinct stratum, recognizing that phenotypic gating strategies developed before CD19- and BCMA-directed therapy may misclassify cells that have lost the very markers used to identify them.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Nine hundred paired specimens will be accrued through an existing cooperative group biology protocol with central processing within 24 hours. Flow will follow a harmonized 10-color panel with a target acquisition of 4 million events and a stated limit of detection of 0.0005 percent; sequencing will use a validated immunoglobulin heavy and kappa chain assay requiring an index specimen with a dominant rearrangement. Concordance will be reported as Cohen kappa overall and stratified by burden decade. Latent class models will be fitted with weakly informative priors and assessed by posterior predictive checks. Surrogacy analysis will use a two-stage weighted regression of trial-level log hazard ratios on log odds ratios, with leave-one-trial-out cross-validation.

title: Engineering CAR T Cells to Overcome Stromal, Metabolic, and Chemokine Barriers in Pancreatic and Ovarian Carcinoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Chimeric antigen receptor T cells that clear marrow disease reliably fail against epithelial carcinoma, and the reasons are not receptor affinity but the terrain. Engineered cells must survive a dense desmoplastic stroma, enter through vessels that lack the adhesion molecules T cells use, function at oxygen tensions below 1 percent, and compete for glucose and glutamine with tumor cells that consume both. This program dissects those barriers one at a time in mesothelin- and MUC16-directed models. We will map the chemokine mismatch between tumor and effector, install a receptor that matches the dominant tumor-derived ligand, insert a dominant-negative TGF-beta receptor to blunt stromal suppression, and test whether metabolic reprogramming through PRODH2 overexpression preserves function under nutrient restriction. Each modification will be evaluated alone and in combination in orthotopic models with intact stroma.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Define the trafficking mismatch. We will quantify chemokine ligands in 60 resected pancreatic and ovarian specimens and compare them with the receptor repertoire of manufactured products, testing the hypothesis that CXCL1 and CXCL8 dominate the tumor while effector cells express predominantly CXCR3. Aim 2. Engineer entry and survival. Products will be modified with CXCR2, with a dominant-negative TGFBR2, or with both, and will be compared for intratumoral density at day 7, functional cytokine output, and control of orthotopic tumors. Aim 3. Sustain function under nutrient and oxygen restriction. Using hypoxia-responsive promoter elements and PRODH2 overexpression, we will test whether engineered cells maintain mitochondrial spare respiratory capacity and resist the terminal exhaustion program that we and others observe by day 14 within tumor tissue.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Objective response rates in unselected solid tumor trials of engineered T cells remain below 10 percent, in contrast with the 40 to 90 percent seen in B-cell malignancies with the same receptor architecture. That gap is the central unsolved problem of the field, and it is not explained by target choice alone: cells that kill efficiently in vitro against the same target fail in vivo. Identifying which barrier is rate-limiting in a given histology would let engineering effort be spent where it matters and would provide the biological rationale for combination designs that are currently assembled by trial and error. The models proposed here retain stroma and an intact vasculature, which is essential because subcutaneous flank implants systematically overestimate engineered cell entry.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: We treat the barriers as separable and testable rather than as a single monolithic obstacle, and we use a factorial design so that interactions between entry, suppression, and metabolic modifications can be estimated rather than assumed. The hypoxia-responsive expression cassette restricts armoring payloads to the tumor bed, which addresses the systemic toxicity that has limited constitutive cytokine armoring. We also introduce paired intravital imaging with photoconvertible reporters, allowing the same engineered cells to be followed from vessel to stroma to tumor nest, so that failure can be attributed to a specific step rather than inferred from an endpoint count of cells per field.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Orthotopic models include KPC-derived pancreatic organoids implanted into the pancreas of immunodeficient mice with reconstituted human immunity, and patient-derived ovarian implants in the peritoneum, with 12 animals per arm and tumor burden followed by bioluminescence twice weekly. Engineered products will be manufactured from three healthy donors per experiment to control for donor variation. Intratumoral density will be quantified by multiplex imaging with segmentation, reported as cells per square millimeter of viable tumor. Metabolic phenotype will be measured by extracellular flux analysis on cells recovered from tissue, with spare respiratory capacity as the primary readout. All comparisons use mixed-effects models with donor as a random effect and Holm correction across the six planned contrasts.

title: Costimulatory Endodomain Design and the Persistence versus Toxicity Tradeoff in Engineered T Cells

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Second-generation receptors carrying CD28 signal faster and harder than those carrying 4-1BB, expand to higher peaks, and are associated with more severe cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxicity, while 4-1BB constructs signal more slowly and remain detectable for years. The tradeoff is treated as a fixed property of the two endodomains, but it is really a property of signal strength and duration, which can be tuned. This program will build a graded series of receptors that vary immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motif number, hinge length, and endodomain composition, and will map how each parameter sets early expansion, terminal differentiation, and cytokine output. The goal is a design rule that predicts, from in vitro signaling kinetics, which construct will retain antitumor activity while lowering peak systemic cytokine production.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Build and characterize a 16-member receptor series varying activation motif number from one to three, hinge and transmembrane composition, and endodomain identity. Aim 2. Relate signaling kinetics to differentiation. Phospho-flow at 2, 10, and 60 minutes after target engagement, followed by 14-day repeat stimulation assays, will test whether the rate of loss of the CD45RA-positive CCR7-positive fraction is a monotone function of early signal amplitude. Aim 3. Test the tradeoff in vivo. NSG mice bearing NALM-6 or Raji tumors will receive equal doses of each construct, with serial quantification of circulating engineered cells, human interleukin 6 and interferon gamma, and survival, in order to identify constructs that preserve tumor control at a peak cytokine level at least 50 percent lower than the CD28 reference.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Toxicity, not efficacy, sets the setting in which these therapies can be delivered. If severe systemic inflammation could be halved without loss of tumor control, administration could move to community centers, older and frailer patients could be treated, and the substantial cost of intensive care support would fall. Current practice chooses between two off-the-shelf endodomains, an extremely coarse instrument. A quantitative design rule linking a measurable in vitro signaling parameter to the in vivo tradeoff would let future constructs be selected before manufacture rather than discovered in the clinic, and would apply equally to receptors directed at targets beyond B-lineage antigens, including those being pursued in epithelial cancers.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Existing comparisons contrast two constructs at a time, which cannot distinguish endodomain identity from signal strength because the two are confounded. A graded 16-member series breaks that confound and permits a dose-response analysis of signal amplitude. We further introduce a repeat-stimulation assay with fixed antigen density as a surrogate for chronic engagement, giving a functional readout of durability that correlates with in vivo behavior far better than single-round cytotoxicity. Finally, we pair each construct with matched cytokine measurements in vivo, so that potency and inflammatory output are measured in the same animals rather than compared across separate experiments.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: All constructs share the FMC63 binder and differ only downstream, and are expressed from a common lentiviral backbone with matched vector copy number verified by droplet digital PCR. Products from six healthy donors will be used for every assay to capture donor variation. Repeat stimulation uses irradiated targets added every 3 days for five rounds, with counts and cytokine output at each round. In vivo, 10 mice per construct per tumor model receive 1e6 cells; engineered cell counts are obtained by flow on 50 microliters of blood twice weekly. Signal amplitude will be summarized as area under the phospho-CD3 zeta curve and related to differentiation and cytokine output by hierarchical modeling with donor-level random intercepts and false discovery control at 5 percent.

title: Real-World Effectiveness, Referral Patterns, and Access to Commercial CAR T-Cell Therapy for Aggressive Lymphoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Registration trials of axicabtagene ciloleucel and tisagenlecleucel enrolled patients who were fit, close to an academic center, and able to wait through manufacturing. Roughly half of patients treated commercially would not have met those eligibility criteria. This program links a national cellular therapy registry to claims and to census-tract measures in order to estimate real-world effectiveness, to describe who is referred and who is not, and to quantify how far the treated population has drifted from the trial population. We will characterize the interval from referral to infusion, the frequency of progression during that interval, the use and intensity of bridging therapy, and the association of treating center volume with severe toxicity and 100-day mortality. The deliverable is an effectiveness estimate with explicit quantification of selection, plus a map of where eligible patients are being lost.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Estimate real-world effectiveness. Using 3200 registry patients infused with a commercial CD19-directed product for aggressive lymphoma, we will estimate 12-month progression-free and overall survival, benchmarked against trial cohorts through standardized mortality ratio and through trial-emulation weighting on eligibility criteria. Aim 2. Describe the referral funnel. Linking claims to registry records, we will estimate the number of patients meeting label indication per region, the fraction referred, and the fraction infused, stratified by insurance, race and ethnicity, rurality, and driving distance to the nearest certified center. Aim 3. Relate structure to outcome. We will model the association of annual center volume and of vein-to-vein interval with grade 3 or higher cytokine release syndrome, with severe neurologic toxicity, with intensive care utilization, and with non-relapse mortality, using hierarchical models with center-level random effects.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Cellular therapy is delivered at roughly 200 certified sites in the United States, and eligibility is decided by referring oncologists who often see one candidate per year. Under those conditions, the dominant determinant of outcome may be whether a patient is referred at all, not which product is chosen. Quantifying loss at each step of the funnel converts an abstract equity concern into targeted intervention points: referral education, apheresis capacity, bridging protocols, or lodging support. Effectiveness estimates that ignore selection also mislead payers and guideline committees. By reporting both a naive and a trial-emulation estimate, this work will make the size of the selection effect explicit rather than leaving it as an unmeasured caveat.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Registry analyses to date describe the treated population only, which cannot address who never arrives. Linking to claims recovers the denominator, allowing the funnel to be estimated rather than assumed. We apply target trial emulation with cloning and censoring to handle the immortal time introduced by the manufacturing interval, a bias that has inflated survival estimates in prior real-world reports. We additionally treat bridging therapy as a time-varying exposure rather than a baseline covariate, which is necessary because bridging intensity responds to disease trajectory during the wait and otherwise induces confounding by indication.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: The registry cohort comprises 3200 adults infused between 2018 and 2023 with complete 12-month follow-up. Linkage to claims will use a deterministic-probabilistic hybrid with an expected match rate above 88 percent. Trial emulation will define eligibility from the pivotal protocols, apply stabilized inverse probability of treatment weights, and report weighted Kaplan-Meier estimates with bootstrap confidence intervals. Funnel estimates will be produced per hospital referral region with small-area smoothing. Center-volume analyses will use restricted cubic splines with three knots and will adjust for case mix, including age, disease burden, lactate dehydrogenase, and prior lines. Sensitivity analyses will quantify the unmeasured confounding required to nullify observed associations using E-values.

title: Infectious Complications and Immune Reconstitution after T-Cell Redirecting Therapy in Myeloma and Lymphoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: T-cell redirecting therapy produces a distinctive and under-characterized immunodeficiency. Patients receiving BCMA-directed bispecific antibodies experience grade 3 or higher infection in roughly 45 percent of cases within the first year, a rate substantially above that seen with CD19-directed cellular therapy, and deaths from infection now exceed deaths from progression in some series during the first 6 months. The drivers are additive: profound and sustained hypogammaglobulinemia, target-driven depletion of normal plasma cells, prolonged neutropenia, T-cell redistribution during step-up dosing, and cumulative corticosteroid exposure for cytokine release syndrome. This program will define the kinetics of humoral and cellular reconstitution across 400 patients on both modalities, identify who requires indefinite immunoglobulin replacement, and test a risk-adapted prophylaxis strategy in a randomized phase 2 study.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Define reconstitution kinetics. Serial immunoglobulin G, specific pneumococcal and tetanus titers, B-cell and plasma cell enumeration, T-cell subsets, and pathogen-specific T-cell responses will be measured at baseline, month 1, month 3, month 6, and month 12 in 400 patients. Aim 2. Identify determinants of severe infection. Using a recurrent-event model, we will test whether cumulative corticosteroid dose, nadir immunoglobulin G, and the duration of neutropenia below 500 per microliter independently predict infection density, and whether the BCMA-directed cohort differs after adjustment. Aim 3. Test risk-adapted prophylaxis. A randomized phase 2 study (NCT05612022) of 180 patients will compare universal immunoglobulin replacement from cycle 1 against replacement triggered by a level below 400 milligrams per deciliter, with grade 3 or higher infection density over 12 months as the primary endpoint.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Efficacy of these agents is no longer the limiting factor for many patients; tolerability over months of continuous dosing is. Because bispecific antibodies are given indefinitely until progression, the immunodeficiency they cause is continuous rather than self-limited, unlike the transient aplasia after a single cellular infusion. Guidance on immunoglobulin replacement, antiviral duration, and vaccine timing is currently extrapolated from transplant practice with little direct evidence. Because these agents are administered in the community once step-up dosing is complete, prescribers outside academic centers need simple, evidence-based rules. Establishing those rules would reduce hospitalization, permit continued treatment at full dose intensity, and remove one of the practical barriers that keeps these agents concentrated in a small number of institutions.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Existing reports count infections as adverse events per patient, which discards timing and repeat events and understates burden in patients with several episodes. We model infection as a recurrent process with treatment exposure as a time-varying covariate, which is the correct structure for continuous therapy. We add functional immunity readouts, specific antibody titers and pathogen-specific T-cell responses, rather than total immunoglobulin alone, because total levels are corrected by replacement and therefore become uninformative once therapy begins. The randomized comparison of universal versus threshold-triggered replacement addresses a question of immediate practical and economic consequence that no registrational program was designed to answer.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Four hundred patients will be enrolled across six centers: 240 receiving teclistamab, elranatamab, or talquetamab, and 160 receiving CD19-directed cellular therapy. Infections will be adjudicated centrally by two infectious disease physicians blinded to cohort, with disagreement resolved by a third. Pathogen-specific T-cell responses will be measured by interferon gamma release against cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, and varicella zoster peptide pools. Recurrent-event analysis will use Andersen-Gill models with robust variance and center-level frailty. The randomized aim uses 1:1 allocation and 90 patients per arm, giving 80 percent power to detect a rate ratio of 0.60 in severe infection density assuming a control rate of 1.1 events per patient-year and 15 percent dropout.

title: Separating Leukemia from Hematopoiesis: Epitope-Edited Grafts for CD33- and CD123-Directed CAR T Cells in Acute Myeloid Leukemia

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Acute myeloid leukemia has no equivalent of CD19: every candidate surface target, including CD33, CD123, CLEC12A, and CD7, is also expressed on normal hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, so effective redirected cytotoxicity produces prolonged marrow aplasia. We propose to break that shared dependence by editing the target epitope out of the donor graft rather than out of the receptor. Base editing of a single codon in CD33 exon 2, or of the receptor-binding surface of the interleukin 3 receptor alpha chain, preserves protein function while abolishing binder recognition, creating a graft that is invisible to the therapy. We will establish editing efficiency and function in human progenitors, demonstrate multilineage reconstitution in mice, and define the duration of redirected therapy that a shielded graft can tolerate.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Engineer shielded progenitors. Adenine base editors delivered as messenger RNA with chemically modified guides will be tested against CD33 and CSF2RA-adjacent epitopes in mobilized CD34-positive cells from 10 donors, with target editing above 85 percent, function retained in colony assays, and unintended edits characterized genome-wide. Aim 2. Demonstrate shielded reconstitution. Mice receiving edited human progenitors will be followed 20 weeks for multilineage output, and then challenged with CD33- or CD123-directed engineered T cells to confirm that edited progenitors survive while leukemic blasts are cleared. Aim 3. Define escape risk. Using primary leukemia grafts, we will determine whether blasts with low target density are selected under therapy, using antibody-binding capacity beads to quantify surface molecules per cell and marrow burden read at a sensitivity of 0.01 percent.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Five-year survival for adults with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia remains below 15 percent, and no redirected cellular therapy has been approved. The single obstacle is shared expression between blasts and normal progenitors, an obstacle that receptor engineering alone cannot solve because affinity tuning cannot separate identical molecules. Shielding the graft inverts the problem: instead of making the therapy more selective, it makes the healthy compartment resistant. Success would open the entire catalogue of myeloid surface targets for redirected therapy, would make repeated dosing feasible, and would provide a template for other lineages in which target sharing has blocked development, including T-lineage leukemia where fratricide has been the corresponding barrier.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Nuclease-based disruption of a target gene removes protein function and can compromise progenitor fitness. Base editing at a single codon changes only the recognized surface, leaving expression and function intact, which is essential for receptors like the interleukin 3 receptor that participate in normal signaling. Our approach also uses paired binder and epitope engineering, selecting variants that lose binder recognition while retaining ligand binding, verified by surface plasmon resonance. Finally, we assess escape prospectively by quantifying molecules per cell rather than by a positive or negative call, because the relevant biology is a continuous density threshold below which redirected killing fails.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Mobilized CD34-positive cells from 10 healthy donors will be electroporated with base editor messenger RNA and guides, with editing quantified by amplicon sequencing and protein assessed by antibody-binding capacity beads. Off-target activity will be assessed by orthogonal genome-wide capture plus RNA editing analysis. NSG-SGM3 mice will receive 2e5 edited progenitors, with 20-week multilineage output measured in blood and marrow, and 10 animals per arm. Primary leukemia grafts from 12 patients will be challenged with engineered T cells at three doses, with burden read serially and surviving blasts recovered for target density measurement. Group comparisons will use mixed models with donor and patient as random effects, with Holm adjustment across the primary contrasts and prespecified futility criteria at the halfway point.

title: Clonal Hematopoiesis, Prolonged Cytopenia, and Second Malignancy Risk after CAR T-Cell Therapy

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: One quarter of patients infused with a CD19-directed product have neutrophil counts below 500 per microliter beyond day 30, and a smaller group remains transfusion dependent for months. Two candidate explanations are rarely separated: an intrinsically damaged marrow, often carrying clonal hematopoiesis after multiple prior lines, and a sustained inflammatory insult from the infusion itself. The distinction matters because one predicts benefit from stem cell boost and the other from anti-inflammatory intervention. We will sequence pre-infusion marrow for clonal hematopoiesis in 600 patients, relate variant identity and allele fraction to the duration of cytopenia, and follow the same cohort for myeloid neoplasms and for T-cell neoplasms arising after infusion, with vector integration analysis performed on any T-lineage event.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Determine whether pre-infusion clonal hematopoiesis explains prolonged cytopenia. Error-corrected sequencing of 61 genes at a variant allele fraction floor of 0.5 percent will be performed on marrow collected before conditioning in 600 patients, and duration of neutropenia will be modeled against variant class, with PPM1D and TP53 variants prespecified as the hypothesis of interest. Aim 2. Separate marrow-intrinsic from inflammation-driven mechanisms by relating cytopenia duration to peak ferritin, C-reactive protein, and interleukin 6 trajectory, with formal mediation analysis. Aim 3. Establish incidence of second malignancy. With 600 patients and a target median follow-up of 4 years, we will estimate cumulative incidence of myeloid neoplasms and of T-cell neoplasms, treating death and relapse as competing risks, and will bank material for integration site analysis on every incident T-lineage event.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Prolonged cytopenia after infusion drives transfusion dependence, infection, and delayed return to systemic therapy, and it is the most common reason for readmission in the first 90 days. Clinicians currently manage it empirically with growth factors, eltrombopag, or an unmanipulated stem cell boost, without evidence about which patients benefit. Separately, reports of T-cell neoplasms arising after infusion have generated regulatory attention out of proportion to the number of documented cases, and the field lacks a denominator-based estimate from a cohort with systematic follow-up and banked material. Producing both an actionable predictor of cytopenia and a rigorous incidence estimate would inform consent discussions and would settle whether observed events exceed what the prior treatment history alone would produce.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Most prior work sequenced apheresis products rather than marrow, which conflates the composition of the collected T cells with the state of the hematopoietic compartment. We sequence the marrow before conditioning chemotherapy, which is the compartment that must recover. Our mediation framework formally partitions the cytopenia effect into a marrow-intrinsic path and an inflammation path rather than adjusting one away. For the second malignancy aim, we prespecify integration site recovery and clonality assessment on incident events, so that a causal attribution to the vector can be made or excluded rather than debated on the basis of temporal association alone.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Six hundred adults treated with commercial CD19-directed products at eight centers will be enrolled consecutively, with marrow collected before fludarabine and cyclophosphamide conditioning. Sequencing uses unique molecular identifiers with a 0.5 percent variant allele fraction floor and a validated 61-gene panel. Cytopenia will be modeled with competing-risk regression for time to sustained neutrophil recovery, adjusting for prior lines, prior transplant, and conditioning intensity. Mediation will use the natural effects framework with bootstrap intervals. For malignancy incidence, cumulative incidence functions with Gray tests will be reported, and 600 patients with 4-year median follow-up give a two-sided 95 percent confidence interval half-width of roughly 0.9 percentage points around an expected 2 percent incidence.

title: Splice Variants, Truncating Mutations, and Lineage Switch Underlie Target-Negative Relapse after Tisagenlecleucel in B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We analyzed 96 paired pre-infusion and relapse specimens from children and young adults treated with tisagenlecleucel for B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Of 41 relapses, 22 were negative for the targeted surface protein. Long-read complementary DNA sequencing identified transcripts lacking exon 2 in 14 of 22, of which 9 also carried a frameshift or nonsense mutation in CD19 exons 2 through 4 at a clonal allele fraction. Three cases showed a switch to a myeloid immunophenotype with acquisition of CD33 and CD11b, loss of CD22 and PAX5 expression, and retention of the original immunoglobulin rearrangement, confirming a common progenitor. Error-corrected sequencing detected the eventual escape variant before infusion in 6 of 19 evaluable cases at fractions between 0.06 and 0.9 percent. Escape was not associated with infused dose but was associated with a shorter interval of detectable vector in blood.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Complete remission rates after infusion of CD19-directed products in relapsed pediatric leukemia exceed 80 percent, but roughly half of subsequent relapses lack the target on the blast surface. Whether such relapses arise from selection of a rare pre-existing subclone or from adaptation under pressure has direct implications for surveillance and for dual-targeting designs. A preclinical comparison of endodomain architecture established that receptors carrying 4-1BB support a longer functional lifespan and a less differentiated effector pool than CD28-containing receptors, which is why 4-1BB constructs dominate in leukemia [PAPER:HEME_CART_P15]. Product composition also matters: a single-cell census of infusion products linked an early-differentiation CD8 population to durable remission [PAPER:HEME_CART_P03]. Neither line of work addressed the tumor side of failure. Here we characterize the tumor-intrinsic routes to escape in a large paired specimen series and ask whether they can be anticipated before infusion.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Ninety-six paired marrow aspirates were collected at infusion and at relapse across four centers under a common protocol. Hybrid-capture sequencing covered 45 B-lineage genes at a mean depth of 1140x. Full-length complementary DNA was sequenced on a Nanopore platform with a median of 480000 aligned reads per sample, and isoforms were quantified after alignment to a curated CD19 transcript set. Single-cell 5-prime libraries with 137 antibody-derived tags were generated for 24 index cases at a target of 8000 cells. Error-corrected amplicon sequencing of CD19 exons 2 through 5 used unique molecular identifiers with a background error rate of 0.02 percent. Surface target density was quantified with antibody-binding capacity beads. Immunoglobulin heavy chain rearrangements were sequenced to establish clonal identity between diagnosis, infusion, and relapse specimens. Associations were tested by Fisher exact tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Twenty-two of 41 relapses were target negative and 19 retained the original immunoglobulin rearrangement. Exon 2 skipping accounted for a median 68 percent of transcripts in the 14 cases carrying it, compared with 4 percent in pre-infusion specimens. Nine cases carried truncating variants, six of which were in trans with a splice variant. Three lineage-switch cases showed a monocytic transcriptional program by single-cell profiling with retention of the leukemic rearrangement. Six of 19 escape variants were detectable before infusion at 0.06 to 0.9 percent. Median time to relapse was 5.4 months for target-negative and 3.1 months for target-positive relapse (P equals 0.008). Vector was detectable in blood for a median of 168 days in target-negative relapse versus 61 days in target-positive relapse (P equals 0.002), and marrow burden at day 28 was below 0.01 percent in 18 of 22 target-negative cases.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Target-negative relapse in this cohort was heterogeneous but dominated by exon 2 loss, frequently compounded by a truncating variant on the second allele, which argues that biallelic events are usually required. The detection of escape variants before infusion in roughly a third of evaluable cases supports selection of pre-existing subclones rather than de novo adaptation, and implies that deep pre-infusion screening could identify children who should receive a dual-targeting construct up front. The contrast between target-negative and target-positive relapse in the duration of detectable vector is informative: target-positive relapse occurred while effector cells were disappearing, consistent with the differentiation-driven loss of function described for CD28-based designs [PAPER:HEME_CART_P15] and with the exhaustion trajectories reported after infusion [PAPER:HEME_CART_P04]. The two failure modes therefore require different remedies, one directed at the tumor and one at the effector.

title: A Bivalent CD19/CD22 Chimeric Antigen Receptor in Relapsed B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia: Phase 1 Dose-Escalation Results

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We report a phase 1 study (NCT03919240) of a single bivalent receptor engaging both CD19 and CD22 through a loop configuration with one 4-1BB endodomain. Thirty-four patients aged 3 to 29 years with relapsed or refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia received fludarabine 30 milligrams per square meter daily for 3 days and cyclophosphamide 500 milligrams per square meter, followed by 1e6 or 3e6 modified cells per kilogram. Complete remission was achieved in 30 of 34 patients, and 28 of 30 had marrow burden below 0.01 percent by immunoglobulin sequencing at day 28. Cytokine release syndrome occurred in 27 patients, grade 3 or higher in 4. At a median follow-up of 19 months, 12-month event-free survival was 61 percent. Of 9 relapses, 2 were negative for both targets, 3 retained both, and 4 lost CD19 alone.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Escape from single-target pressure is the dominant cause of relapse in this population. Detailed characterization of paired specimens showed that exon 2 splice variants and truncating mutations, frequently biallelic, account for the majority of target-negative relapses, and that the responsible subclone can sometimes be detected before infusion [PAPER:HEME_CART_P01]. Sequential targeting with a second product after relapse is logistically difficult and gives the tumor time to expand. Simultaneous engagement of two independent lineage markers should raise the genetic cost of escape, but earlier attempts using two separate receptors encountered unbalanced surface expression and vector packaging limits. A loop design places both binders in one polypeptide with a single signaling module. Accurate depth-of-response assessment in this setting requires a genomic assay, since phenotypic gating can misclassify blasts that have lost the markers used to identify them [PAPER:HEME_CART_P11].

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Eligible patients had 5 percent or more marrow blasts or extramedullary disease after at least two prior regimens, including prior blinatumomab in 14 and prior inotuzumab in 9. Cells were manufactured over 9 days from a fresh apheresis product with a median vector copy number of 2.4 per cell. Dose escalation followed a 3 plus 3 design at 1e6 and 3e6 cells per kilogram. Toxicity was graded by ASTCT consensus criteria. Marrow was assessed at day 28, month 3, and every 3 months by an 10-color panel and by immunoglobulin heavy chain sequencing with a floor of 10^-6. Surface CD19 and CD22 density on relapse blasts was measured with antibody-binding capacity beads. Modified cells in blood were quantified by droplet digital PCR against the vector junction.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Thirty of 34 patients entered complete remission, including 8 of 10 with prior blinatumomab exposure. Twenty-eight of 30 responders had undetectable marrow burden at 10^-6 by sequencing at day 28; three of these were scored positive between 0.01 and 0.05 percent by the phenotypic panel, and all three remained in remission. Cytokine release syndrome occurred in 27 patients at a median onset of day 3, with tocilizumab given to 19 and vasopressors required in 4. Grade 3 or higher neurologic events occurred in 3 patients. Peak transgene copies reached a median of 78000 per microgram of DNA at day 11, and transgene remained detectable at 12 months in 17 of 26 evaluable patients. Among 9 relapses, 4 showed isolated CD19 loss with retained CD22 at a median density of 3100 molecules per cell.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Dual engagement did not abolish escape but changed its character: isolated CD19 loss with retained CD22 was the most common pattern, indicating that the CD22 arm of the loop construct did not deliver sufficient signal at the observed surface densities. This is consistent with reports that CD22-directed activity falls sharply below roughly 2000 molecules per cell. The high concordance between the sequencing and phenotypic assessments at day 28, with discordance confined to the 0.01 to 0.05 percent range, matches the pattern described in a paired-assay analysis of this disease [PAPER:HEME_CART_P11]. Notably, activity was preserved after prior blinatumomab, arguing against a durable loss of the CD19 epitope from that exposure. Future designs should raise the sensitivity of the second arm rather than add a third binder, and should be evaluated with a genomic depth-of-response endpoint.

title: A Single-Cell Census of Axicabtagene Ciloleucel Infusion Products Identifies an Early-Differentiation CD8 Population Associated with Durable Remission

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We profiled 84 axicabtagene ciloleucel infusion products by 5-prime single-cell transcriptome capture with surface protein tagging and paired receptor sequencing, and related composition to outcome in patients with relapsed large B-cell lymphoma. An early-differentiation CD8 population expressing TCF7, IL7R, SELL, and CD27 comprised a median of 18 percent of transfused cells in patients free of progression at 12 months versus 6 percent in those progressing within 90 days. A second population co-expressing TOX, ENTPD1, HAVCR2, and LAG3 showed the inverse pattern. In a multivariable model adjusting for tumor bulk and lactate dehydrogenase, each interquartile increase in the early-differentiation fraction corresponded to a hazard ratio of 0.54 for progression. Clonotype tracking showed that expanding clones at day 14 derived preferentially from the early-differentiation compartment, with a median enrichment of 4.1-fold.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Roughly 40 percent of patients treated with axicabtagene ciloleucel for aggressive lymphoma remain free of progression beyond 2 years, and clinical covariates explain only a modest share of that variation. Peak expansion in blood correlates with response but is measurable only after treatment. Attention has therefore turned to the transfused product itself, where cellular composition is fixed at release and is in principle modifiable through manufacturing. Bulk phenotyping of a handful of markers has produced inconsistent results, in part because the relevant populations are defined by combinations of transcriptional regulators rather than by single surface proteins. A parallel line of work has shown that dysfunctional programs in engineered T cells are governed by TOX and its downstream network [PAPER:HEME_CART_P04], while endodomain composition sets the rate at which cells traverse from an early to a terminal state [PAPER:HEME_CART_P15]. We asked whether the composition of the transfused product carries information about eventual outcome.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Aliquots of 84 products were collected at release under an approved amendment and cryopreserved. Libraries were prepared with 10x Genomics 5-prime chemistry, 137 oligonucleotide-conjugated antibodies, and paired alpha and beta chain enrichment, targeting 8000 cells per sample. After quality filtering, 612000 cells were retained. Clustering used shared-nearest-neighbor graphs with batch correction across processing days. Compositional fractions were modeled by Dirichlet-multinomial regression against progression-free survival with adjustment for tumor bulk, lactate dehydrogenase, and prior lines. Serial blood at days 7, 14, 28 and month 3 was available for 46 patients and was profiled identically. Clonotypes were matched exactly on complementarity-determining region 3 nucleotide sequence, and enrichment of product-derived clones was assessed against a permutation null constructed by shuffling clone labels within each patient.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Nine transcriptional states were recovered. The early-differentiation CD8 state, defined by TCF7, IL7R, SELL, and CD27 with low ENTPD1, accounted for a median 18 percent of cells in the 31 patients free of progression at 12 months versus 6 percent in the 24 progressing within 90 days (P less than 0.001). The dysfunctional state co-expressing TOX, HAVCR2, LAG3, and ENTPD1 accounted for a median 21 percent versus 9 percent in the opposite direction. Each interquartile increase in the early-differentiation fraction gave an adjusted hazard ratio of 0.54 (95 percent confidence interval 0.37 to 0.79). Clones detectable at day 14 derived from the early-differentiation compartment with a 4.1-fold enrichment. Transgene remained detectable at 6 months in 21 of 27 patients whose product exceeded the median early-differentiation fraction, versus 8 of 26 below it.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Product composition at release carries substantial information about eventual outcome, and the informative feature is a differentiation state rather than a simple CD4 to CD8 ratio. The clonotype tracking result is the strongest evidence to date that the cells doing the work in vivo are drawn from a specific compartment present before transfer, which reframes manufacturing as a selection problem. Our findings complement work showing that the dysfunctional program is initiated by TOX and consolidated at the chromatin level [PAPER:HEME_CART_P04], since we observe the transcriptional signature of that program already present at release in a subset of products. Limitations include a single manufacturing platform and a modest number of early progression events. Prospective testing of release criteria that incorporate compositional readouts is warranted before composition is used to route patients.

title: TOX and TCF7 Specify Divergent Fates of CD19-Directed CAR T Cells after Infusion and Define an Irreversible Commitment Point

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Chronic receptor engagement drives engineered T cells into a dysfunctional state, but when that state becomes fixed is unknown. We tracked CD19-directed cells in 38 patients from infusion through month 3 using paired single-cell transcriptome and chromatin accessibility profiling of sorted transgene-positive cells. Cells recovered at day 7 showed a broad distribution of states, whereas by day 21 the majority of cells in non-responding patients occupied a TOX-high, TCF7-low state with closed accessibility at IL7R and SELL enhancers and opened accessibility at PDCD1, HAVCR2, and ENTPD1 loci. In vitro, transient BATF3 overexpression during manufacture reduced acquisition of the TOX-high state by 46 percent and increased 21-day expansion 2.8-fold, but the same intervention applied after day 14 of chronic stimulation had no effect, defining a window in which fate remains modifiable.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Loss of function under sustained antigen exposure limits engineered T-cell therapy in both leukemia and epithelial cancer. Transcriptional and epigenetic circuits underlying this state have been mapped in chronic viral infection, and TOX has emerged as a central node, but whether the same circuit governs engineered cells in patients, and whether it is reversible, remains unclear. Product composition is one determinant: a single-cell census of infusion products showed that an early-differentiation CD8 population is enriched in patients with durable remission [PAPER:HEME_CART_P03]. Receptor architecture is another, since endodomain identity sets the rate of differentiation under repeated stimulation [PAPER:HEME_CART_P15]. Here we ask when the dysfunctional program becomes epigenetically fixed in vivo, because the answer determines whether intervention must occur during manufacture or can be applied after infusion.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Blood was collected at days 7, 14, 21, 28 and month 3 from 38 patients receiving CD19-directed products for lymphoma or leukemia. Transgene-positive cells were sorted with an anti-idiotype reagent to a purity above 92 percent. Paired transcriptome and transposase-accessible chromatin libraries were prepared from the same nuclei. Differential accessibility was assessed with a negative binomial model at a false discovery rate of 5 percent, and regulator activity was inferred from motif enrichment within differentially accessible regions. For manufacturing experiments, healthy donor cells were transduced and stimulated with irradiated NALM-6 every 3 days for seven rounds; BATF3 was expressed from a doxycycline-inducible cassette and induced either during days 0 to 5 or days 14 to 19. Expansion, cytokine output, and marker expression were measured at each round.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: A total of 214000 transgene-positive cells were profiled. At day 7, state entropy was high and did not differ by outcome. By day 21, cells from the 17 non-responding patients occupied the TOX-high, TCF7-low state at a median frequency of 64 percent versus 22 percent in responders (P less than 0.001). Accessibility at the IL7R and SELL enhancer regions fell by a median of 2.4-fold between day 7 and day 21 in non-responders, and accessibility gains at PDCD1 and ENTPD1 preceded transcript increases by roughly a week. Early BATF3 induction reduced acquisition of the TOX-high state from 58 to 31 percent and increased cumulative expansion 2.8-fold, while late induction produced no measurable change in state distribution, expansion, or interferon gamma output.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: These data locate an epigenetic commitment point between day 7 and day 21 after infusion, after which the dysfunctional program is no longer reversible by a regulator that is effective earlier. The practical implication is that interventions intended to preserve function must be applied during manufacture or in the first week, not at the time of clinical progression. Our observations extend the compositional finding that an early-differentiation population in the product is associated with durable remission [PAPER:HEME_CART_P03], by showing that descendants of that population resist the accessibility changes we describe. The dependence of the trajectory rate on endodomain identity [PAPER:HEME_CART_P15] suggests that construct design and manufacturing intervention act on the same axis, and may not be additive. Limitations include the absence of tumor-infiltrating samples and reliance on peripheral blood as a proxy compartment.

title: Biallelic TNFRSF17 Loss and Elevated Shed Receptor Define Two Routes to Teclistamab Failure in Relapsed Multiple Myeloma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We studied 74 patients with relapsed multiple myeloma treated with teclistamab, with sorted plasma cells and marrow T cells banked at baseline, best response, and progression. Among 52 progression specimens, 11 carried biallelic TNFRSF17 events, comprising 7 homozygous deletions and 4 combinations of deletion with a truncating variant, and all 11 showed absent surface staining. An additional 9 patients had serum shed receptor above 400 nanograms per milliliter at progression with retained surface expression. In the remaining 32, the target was intact and the dominant change was on the effector side: CD8 cells co-expressing PD-1, TIGIT, and CD160 rose from a median 12 percent at baseline to 41 percent at progression, with interferon gamma and tumor necrosis factor double-producing fractions falling by half. Baseline coinhibitory receptor burden was associated with duration of response (hazard ratio 1.9 per 10 percent increase).

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Bispecific antibodies engaging BCMA produce responses in roughly 60 percent of triple-class exposed patients, but nearly all responses are eventually lost. Because these agents are given continuously, the failure biology differs from that of a single cellular infusion. Target-negative escape has been characterized most thoroughly in B-lineage leukemia, where exon-skipping transcripts and truncating mutations in the targeted gene were recovered from paired relapse specimens and were sometimes detectable before treatment [PAPER:HEME_CART_P01]. Whether analogous genomic events explain failure in myeloma, or whether effector dysfunction dominates, has not been established in a series with matched baseline material. The distinction is clinically decisive: switching targets is rational for the former and futile for the latter. We therefore assembled a longitudinal cohort with sorted tumor and effector compartments at three fixed timepoints.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Seventy-four patients receiving teclistamab at two centers consented to serial marrow sampling. Plasma cells were enriched by CD138 selection and sorted to above 95 percent purity; whole-exome and targeted sequencing covered TNFRSF17, GPRC5D, FCRH5, and 118 myeloma genes at 800x. Copy number was called from off-target reads and confirmed by droplet digital PCR. Serum shed receptor was measured by electrochemiluminescence with a lower limit of quantification of 0.8 nanograms per milliliter. Marrow T cells were profiled by 42-marker mass cytometry in all patients and by 10x Genomics 5-prime libraries with antibody-derived tags in 22. Depth of response was assessed by immunoglobulin clonotype sequencing at a floor of 10^-6. Duration of response was modeled by Cox regression with baseline covariates and with tumor-side resistance class as a time-fixed stratum.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Fifty-two patients progressed at a median of 11.4 months. Biallelic TNFRSF17 events occurred in 11 of 52, none of which were detectable at baseline by droplet digital PCR at a 0.2 percent floor. Shed receptor exceeded 400 nanograms per milliliter in 9 additional patients and correlated inversely with reduction in involved free light chain (Spearman rho equals -0.58). In the 32 target-intact progressions, the frequency of CD8 cells expressing three or more coinhibitory receptors rose from 12 to 41 percent, polyfunctional fractions halved, and single-cell profiling showed increased TOX and ENTPD1 transcripts. Baseline coinhibitory burden above the median predicted shorter response (median 7.2 versus 16.8 months, P equals 0.003). Undetectable disease at 10^-6 was reached by 19 patients, whose median duration of response was 26.1 months.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Two thirds of teclistamab failures in this series occurred with the target intact, which argues against reflexive target switching as a universal strategy and identifies effector dysfunction as the larger problem. The genomic events we recovered mirror those described in leukemia in requiring loss of both alleles [PAPER:HEME_CART_P01], but differ in that we found no evidence of pre-existing subclones at our detection floor, suggesting selection from a smaller founder population or acquisition under pressure. Depth of response measured by clonotype sequencing separated durable from transient benefit, consistent with the trial-level relationship between response depth and progression-free survival reported in this disease [PAPER:HEME_CART_P12]. Prospective assignment of resistance class at progression, followed by randomization between target switch and mechanism switch, is the necessary next step.

title: Talquetamab after Failure of BCMA-Directed Therapy: Response, Target Dynamics, and Toxicity in a Prospective Cohort

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We treated 88 patients with relapsed multiple myeloma who had progressed on a BCMA-directed bispecific antibody or cellular product with the GPRC5D-directed bispecific antibody talquetamab. The overall response rate was 63 percent and was 71 percent among 24 patients with documented biallelic loss of the prior target, versus 55 percent among those whose prior target was intact (P equals 0.04). Median progression-free survival was 9.8 months. Undetectable marrow disease at 10^-5 was achieved by 21 patients. Cytokine release syndrome occurred in 68 percent, grade 3 or higher in 3 percent, and was managed with tocilizumab in 44 patients. Characteristic on-target effects included dysgeusia in 61 percent, nail changes in 48 percent, and weight loss exceeding 5 percent in 27 percent. Grade 3 or higher infection occurred in 24 percent over 12 months, lower than contemporaneous BCMA-directed cohorts.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Once a patient progresses on therapy directed at BCMA, the next choice is unguided. A longitudinal resistance analysis found that only a minority of teclistamab failures involve loss of the target, while most occur with the target intact and with accumulation of CD8 cells carrying multiple coinhibitory receptors and reduced polyfunctionality [PAPER:HEME_CART_P05]. If that partition is real, patients whose target is lost should benefit from switching to a different surface molecule, whereas those with intact target may not, because the limiting factor is the effector compartment they still possess.
