GPRC5D is expressed on malignant plasma cells and on keratinized tissue but not on the target of prior therapy, making it a clean test of that hypothesis. We prospectively treated a cohort stratified by prior resistance class.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Eighty-eight patients enrolled at four centers had progressed on teclistamab, elranatamab, or a BCMA-directed cellular product. Archived progression marrow was assayed for TNFRSF17 copy number by droplet digital PCR and for surface expression by antibody-binding capacity beads; patients were classified as target-lost or target-intact before starting talquetamab. Talquetamab was given at 0.8 milligrams per kilogram every 2 weeks after step-up dosing. Response was assessed by International Myeloma Working Group criteria, and depth of response by immunoglobulin clonotype sequencing at a floor of 10^-6 in patients achieving complete response. Toxicity was graded by ASTCT and CTCAE version 5 criteria. Infections were adjudicated centrally. Response by resistance class was compared by Fisher exact test, and time-to-event endpoints by Cox models adjusting for prior lines and cytogenetic risk.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Fifty-five of 88 patients responded. Among 24 classified as target-lost, 17 responded, versus 35 of 64 with intact prior target (P equals 0.04). Median progression-free survival was 9.8 months overall and 13.2 months in the target-lost group. Twenty-one patients reached undetectable disease at 10^-5, and 12 at 10^-6. GPRC5D surface density at baseline did not correlate with response (rho equals 0.11), but 6 of 19 evaluable progression specimens showed loss of GPRC5D expression, of which 4 carried biallelic GPRC5D deletions and 2 showed promoter hypermethylation with retained copy number. Cytokine release syndrome occurred in 60 patients, almost entirely during step-up dosing, with a median duration of 2 days. Grade 3 or higher infection occurred in 21 patients, and 34 received immunoglobulin replacement.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Switching the targeted surface molecule works best in exactly the patients predicted to benefit by mechanism, supporting prospective resistance classification at progression rather than empirical sequencing. The 55 percent response rate in the target-intact group nonetheless shows that effector dysfunction is not absolute and that a fresh binder can recruit residual function. Two routes to GPRC5D loss appeared in our progression specimens, one genomic and one transcriptional, the latter unusual among reported escape mechanisms for T-cell redirecting therapy and consistent with the promoter methylation described in earlier resistance surveys. Lower infection density than contemporaneous BCMA-directed cohorts is expected because normal plasma cells do not express this target, but the 24 percent rate of severe infection remains substantial and supports routine immunoglobulin monitoring.

title: Interleukin 1 Beta and a Rising Angiopoietin 2 to Angiopoietin 1 Ratio Precede Severe Neurotoxicity after CD19-Directed CAR T-Cell Therapy

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We sampled 133 adults receiving CD19-directed products at 12-hour intervals through day 7, with cerebrospinal fluid at day 3 and at symptom onset. Grade 3 or higher neurotoxicity occurred in 34 patients. Interleukin 1 beta rose a median of 22 hours before the first neurologic sign and 14 hours before the interleukin 6 peak. The ratio of angiopoietin 2 to angiopoietin 1 measured before infusion was 2.9 in patients who later developed severe neurotoxicity versus 1.1 in those who did not, and a post-infusion ratio above 4 identified severe events with 81 percent sensitivity and 74 percent specificity. Cerebrospinal fluid at symptom onset showed protein above 60 milligrams per deciliter in 28 of 34 and interleukin 1 beta concentrations exceeding paired serum. Tocilizumab administration did not alter the trajectory of neurologic signs despite abrogating fever.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Neurologic toxicity after infusion is the leading cause of intensive care admission in this population and is only partially coupled to cytokine release syndrome: it often begins as fever resolves, and interleukin 6 receptor blockade, which reliably reverses hemodynamic instability, does not reverse encephalopathy. That dissociation suggests an upstream initiator that is not the interleukin 6 axis. Products carrying CD28 endodomains reach higher peak expansion and are associated with more severe neurologic events than 4-1BB constructs, a difference traced to early signal amplitude in a graded receptor series [PAPER:HEME_CART_P15]. Composition of the transfused product also shapes the magnitude and timing of in vivo expansion [PAPER:HEME_CART_P03]. We tested whether interleukin 1 beta released from CD14-positive cells, and subsequent endothelial activation, order the events that culminate in barrier failure.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: One hundred thirty-three adults with aggressive lymphoma at two centers were sampled every 12 hours from day 0 through day 7 and daily thereafter to day 14. Ninety-two analytes were measured on a validated multiplex platform with intra-assay coefficients of variation below 12 percent. Angiopoietin 1 and 2 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Cerebrospinal fluid was obtained at day 3 in 71 patients and at symptom onset in 34. Neurotoxicity was graded by ASTCT consensus criteria applied prospectively by two assessors. Temporal ordering was assessed by fitting subject-specific spline trajectories and comparing inflection times with a paired bootstrap. Mediation analysis used inverse probability weighting with 2000 bootstrap replicates. Cellular sources were identified by intracellular staining of cryopreserved samples at three timepoints in 40 patients.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Interleukin 1 beta inflected at a median of 22 hours before the first neurologic sign, preceding interleukin 6 by 14 hours and ferritin by 30 hours. Among 34 severe events, the pre-infusion angiopoietin ratio was 2.9 versus 1.1 (P less than 0.001), and a post-infusion ratio above 4 gave an area under the curve of 0.83. Mediation analysis attributed 61 percent of the association between interleukin 1 beta and severe neurotoxicity to the subsequent angiopoietin shift. Intracellular staining localized interleukin 1 beta production to CD14-positive cells, which expanded 3.4-fold between day 1 and day 4. Cerebrospinal fluid protein exceeded 60 milligrams per deciliter in 28 of 34 severe cases. Tocilizumab reduced fever within 12 hours in 46 of 51 treated patients but did not shorten neurologic events (median 5.5 versus 5.1 days).

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: The ordering we observe places interleukin 1 beta upstream of both the interleukin 6 peak and endothelial destabilization, which explains why receptor blockade of the latter pathway is ineffective for encephalopathy. The angiopoietin ratio is attractive because it is measurable before infusion and identifies a susceptible endothelium rather than an inflammatory state, allowing risk to be assigned at the time of the treatment decision. Our findings support prophylactic interleukin 1 receptor antagonism, which in preclinical work abrogates both syndromes without impairing tumor control. The association of higher-amplitude signaling constructs with severe events [PAPER:HEME_CART_P15] fits a model in which the magnitude of the initial burst sets the severity of downstream endothelial injury. Limitations include the absence of a comparator with 4-1BB constructs of sufficient size and reliance on peripheral sampling for a compartmentalized process.

title: Prophylactic Anakinra Reduces Severe Neurotoxicity after Axicabtagene Ciloleucel: A Single-Arm Phase 2 Study

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Sixty adults with relapsed large B-cell lymphoma received anakinra 200 milligrams subcutaneously daily from day 0 through day 10 alongside standard axicabtagene ciloleucel (NCT04150913). The primary endpoint, grade 3 or higher immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, occurred in 8 of 60 patients (13 percent), compared with a prespecified historical rate of 28 percent (one-sided P equals 0.008). Any-grade cytokine release syndrome occurred in 47 patients and grade 3 or higher in 3. Tocilizumab was administered to 29 patients and corticosteroids to 21, compared with 68 percent corticosteroid use in the historical cohort. Peak interleukin 1 receptor antagonist levels confirmed target engagement, and serum interleukin 6 and ferritin peaks were reduced by 44 and 38 percent respectively. Overall response was 82 percent and 12-month progression-free survival 46 percent, similar to historical controls, with peak transgene expansion unchanged.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Management of neurologic toxicity is currently reactive, escalating corticosteroids once encephalopathy appears, an approach that shortens events but has been associated with inferior progression-free survival in several series. A prospective sampling study established that interleukin 1 beta rises roughly a day before the first neurologic sign and before the interleukin 6 peak, and that a rising angiopoietin 2 to angiopoietin 1 ratio mediates most of its association with severe events [PAPER:HEME_CART_P07]. That ordering predicts that blocking interleukin 1 signaling before symptoms should prevent, rather than merely truncate, the syndrome. Because anakinra has a short half-life and does not impair engineered cell expansion in preclinical models, a fixed 11-day prophylactic course is feasible. Real-world series show that severe neurologic events are the dominant driver of intensive care utilization and length of stay after this product [PAPER:HEME_CART_P16].

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Eligible patients were adults with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma after two or more lines, planned for standard axicabtagene ciloleucel. A Simon two-stage design with a futility look at 20 patients tested a reduction in severe neurotoxicity from 28 to 12 percent with 90 percent power. Toxicity was graded prospectively by ASTCT criteria with central adjudication of all grade 2 or higher neurologic events. Cytokines were measured daily through day 14. Transgene copies were quantified by droplet digital PCR. Corticosteroids and tocilizumab were given per institutional algorithm, unchanged from the historical period. The historical comparator comprised 96 consecutive patients treated at the same centers in the preceding 30 months, with identical grading and adjudication procedures.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Eight of 60 patients had grade 3 or higher neurotoxicity, and no patient had a grade 4 event; median duration among affected patients was 3 days versus 6 days historically. Cytokine release syndrome of any grade occurred in 47 patients with median onset day 2 and median duration 3 days. Corticosteroid exposure fell from a historical median cumulative dexamethasone equivalent of 60 milligrams to 20 milligrams. Peak interleukin 6 was 118 versus 210 picograms per milliliter and peak ferritin 1420 versus 2290 nanograms per milliliter. Median peak transgene expansion was 42000 copies per microgram of DNA, not different from the historical cohort (P equals 0.61). Intensive care admission occurred in 7 patients versus 22 percent historically. Overall response was 82 percent with 12-month progression-free survival of 46 percent.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Prophylactic interleukin 1 receptor antagonism roughly halved severe neurotoxicity without measurable loss of expansion or efficacy, supporting the causal ordering inferred from serial sampling [PAPER:HEME_CART_P07]. The reduction in corticosteroid exposure may matter as much as the primary endpoint, since cumulative steroid dose has been repeatedly associated with inferior outcomes in observational series. A single-arm design with a historical comparator is the principal limitation; grading drift is mitigated by identical adjudication procedures, but ascertainment cannot be fully equalized. Because the intervention is inexpensive, subcutaneous, and short, a positive randomized confirmation would make outpatient administration plausible for a substantially larger fraction of patients, an issue of particular importance given documented shortfalls in the number of patients who reach infusion at all.

title: TRAC- and B2M-Disrupted Allogeneic CD19-Directed CAR T Cells in Relapsed B-Cell Malignancy: A First-in-Human Phase 1 Study

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Twenty-six patients, 15 with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and 11 with aggressive lymphoma, received a banked donor-derived CD19-directed product in which TRAC and B2M were disrupted by CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein before lentiviral transduction. Residual receptor-positive cells were below 0.4 percent after depletion in all lots. Conditioning comprised fludarabine, cyclophosphamide, and alemtuzumab. Complete remission occurred in 18 of 26 patients at day 28, with marrow burden below 10^-4 in 15. Cytokine release syndrome occurred in 21 patients, grade 3 or higher in 3; grade 3 neurotoxicity occurred in 2. No patient developed acute graft-versus-host disease of grade 2 or higher. Transgene was detectable at a median of 32 days and was undetectable beyond day 60 in 22 of 26 patients, and 9 of 18 responders proceeded to allogeneic transplant.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Autologous manufacture requires 3 to 5 weeks and fails outright in a meaningful minority of heavily pretreated patients, so a banked product available on demand would change practice. Two immunologic barriers must be removed simultaneously: donor receptor-mediated attack on host tissue, addressed by disrupting the constant region of the endogenous receptor, and host clearance of the graft, addressed here by removing surface class I and by intensified serotherapy. Engineered cell fate after transfer is governed by differentiation trajectories that become fixed within weeks [PAPER:HEME_CART_P04], and endodomain architecture sets the rate at which that occurs [PAPER:HEME_CART_P15], both of which bear on how long a donor product can be expected to function before it is cleared. Because target-negative relapse remains common after single-target pressure [PAPER:HEME_CART_P01], depth and durability of remission were assessed with a genomic assay.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Cells from three healthy donors were activated, electroporated with ribonucleoprotein complexes targeting TRAC and B2M, transduced with a lentiviral vector encoding a 4-1BB-containing CD19-directed receptor, expanded, and depleted of residual receptor-positive cells magnetically. Editing efficiency, translocation frequency by droplet digital PCR, and integration site distribution were characterized for each lot as part of release testing and long-term follow-up. Patients received fludarabine 30 milligrams per square meter for 4 days, cyclophosphamide 60 milligrams per square meter for 2 days, and alemtuzumab 1 milligram per kilogram total. Dose levels were 1e6, 3e6, and 1e7 cells per kilogram in a 3 plus 3 design. Marrow was assessed by an 10-color panel and immunoglobulin sequencing. Long-term follow-up includes annual integration site recovery from blood for 15 years.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median editing was 92 percent at TRAC and 88 percent at B2M, with reciprocal translocations detected at 0.08 to 0.3 percent of alleles. Eighteen of 26 patients achieved complete remission, 15 with marrow burden below 10^-4 at day 28. Response rates were 12 of 15 in leukemia and 6 of 11 in lymphoma. Cytokine release syndrome occurred in 21 patients at a median onset of day 4; 14 received tocilizumab. Two patients had grade 3 neurotoxicity, both resolving within 4 days. No grade 2 or higher acute graft-versus-host disease occurred. Transgene expansion peaked at a median of 8200 copies per microgram at day 12, roughly an order of magnitude below reported autologous ranges, and became undetectable beyond day 60 in 22 patients. Six of eight non-responders had recovered host lymphocyte counts above 300 per microliter by day 14.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: A banked edited product produced remissions at rates approaching autologous therapy, but the window of activity was short, and recovery of host lymphocytes was associated with failure, implicating clearance rather than intrinsic effector deficiency. The practical consequence is that responses must be consolidated, and half of our responders proceeded to transplant. Extending graft survival will require engineering rather than more serotherapy, since deeper depletion carries infection risk that was already evident in this cohort. Because differentiation state at transfer conditions how much expansion is achievable in a short window [PAPER:HEME_CART_P04], donor selection and shortened culture are likely to matter more here than in the autologous setting. Integration site monitoring and annual sampling are in place to detect any clonal proliferation arising from vector insertion.

title: HLA-E Single-Chain Trimer Knock-In at the B2M Locus Extends Survival of Donor-Derived CAR T Cells against Natural Killer Clearance

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Donor-derived engineered T cells lacking surface class I escape host CD8 recognition but become susceptible to natural killer cells that sense missing self. We inserted an HLA-E single-chain trimer bearing a VMAPRTLVL peptide into the disrupted B2M locus of CD19-directed products, coupling the evasion cassette to the edit that creates vulnerability. Knock-in cells resisted killing by purified natural killer cells from 12 mismatched donors, with median specific lysis falling from 48 to 11 percent at an effector-to-target ratio of 5 to 1. In mice reconstituted with mismatched human immune systems, knock-in cells remained detectable for a median of 34 days versus 12 days for class I-null controls, and cleared Raji tumors in 9 of 12 animals versus 3 of 12. Circulating knock-in cells retained a CD45RA-positive CCR7-positive fraction of 31 percent at day 21.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: The first clinical experience with banked edited products showed that remissions were achieved at rates approaching autologous therapy, but the transgene became undetectable within 2 months in the great majority of patients, and recovery of host lymphocytes was associated with failure [PAPER:HEME_CART_P09]. Deeper serotherapy is not a viable answer because it increases infection risk. Engineering the graft to resist clearance is the alternative. Removing surface class I prevents recognition by host CD8 cells but licenses natural killer cells, so the evasion strategy must restore an inhibitory signal without restoring the classical presentation that provokes rejection. Non-classical HLA-E engages NKG2A and is a natural candidate. Because a short functional window constrains how much expansion can occur before commitment to a terminal state [PAPER:HEME_CART_P04], extending graft survival may also change the quality of the response.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Healthy donor cells were electroporated with ribonucleoprotein targeting B2M together with an adeno-associated virus donor template encoding the single-chain trimer, then transduced with a lentiviral vector encoding a 4-1BB-containing CD19-directed receptor. Knock-in was quantified by junction PCR and surface staining. Natural killer cells were purified from 12 mismatched donors and used in 4-hour and 16-hour cytotoxicity assays across effector-to-target ratios of 1 to 1 through 10 to 1. Mice were reconstituted with mismatched CD34-positive cells, engrafted with Raji tumors, and given 5e6 engineered cells, 12 animals per arm, with weekly bioluminescence and biweekly blood sampling. Differentiation was assessed by surface panels and by 5-prime single-cell libraries on recovered cells at day 21. Group comparisons used mixed models with donor as a random effect.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Knock-in efficiency was 62 percent with surface trimer detected on 58 percent of cells after selection. Median specific lysis by mismatched natural killer cells fell from 48 percent for class I-null controls to 11 percent for knock-in cells at a 5 to 1 ratio, and blockade of NKG2A abolished the protection, confirming mechanism. In reconstituted mice, engineered cells remained detectable for a median of 34 versus 12 days, and tumor clearance occurred in 9 of 12 versus 3 of 12 animals (P equals 0.02). Recovered knock-in cells retained a CD45RA-positive CCR7-positive fraction of 31 percent at day 21 versus 12 percent for controls, with lower TOX and ENTPD1 transcript levels. No enrichment of cells with reciprocal translocations was observed at day 21 relative to the infused product.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Coupling the inhibitory ligand to the very locus whose disruption creates susceptibility ensures that cells lacking classical presentation also display the protective molecule, avoiding the mixed populations that random integration produces. The tripling of graft survival in reconstituted animals addresses the specific failure mode observed clinically, in which host lymphocyte recovery coincided with loss of the transgene [PAPER:HEME_CART_P09]. Retention of a less differentiated circulating fraction suggests that a longer window is not simply more of the same cells but a different qualitative trajectory, consistent with a commitment point reached within weeks of transfer [PAPER:HEME_CART_P04]. Limitations include reliance on reconstituted animals with incomplete lymphoid architecture and the absence of repeated dosing, which is the setting in which sensitization is most likely to matter clinically.

title: Paired Comparison of Immunoglobulin Clonotype Sequencing and Ten-Color Flow Cytometry for Residual Disease Detection in B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We assayed 612 paired marrow specimens from 284 patients with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia by a standardized 10-color flow cytometric panel and by immunoglobulin heavy and kappa chain sequencing. Overall agreement was 91 percent (Cohen kappa 0.79). Discordance concentrated between 0.001 and 0.01 percent, where sequencing detected disease in 68 specimens scored negative by flow, and flow detected disease in 9 scored negative by sequencing. Hemodilution, quantified by mast cell content, accounted for 41 percent of flow-negative discordance. Among patients negative by both assays at end of consolidation, 5-year event-free survival was 84 percent, versus 61 percent for those positive by sequencing alone and 38 percent for those positive by both. A latent class model without a gold standard estimated sensitivity of 0.93 for sequencing and 0.71 for flow at burdens between 0.001 and 0.01 percent.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Depth of response now determines consolidation intensity in this disease, and increasingly serves as a primary endpoint in early-phase cellular therapy studies, where remission depth at day 28 is reported as the principal efficacy measure [PAPER:HEME_CART_P09]. Two assays dominate practice and are treated as interchangeable, although they measure different things: one counts cells with an aberrant surface profile, the other counts genomic rearrangements. Interchangeability has never been tested at scale with a design that avoids treating either assay as truth. Assay choice has become more consequential since the introduction of therapies directed at lineage surface molecules, because blasts may lose the very markers used for gating; paired specimen analyses have documented exactly such loss at relapse [PAPER:HEME_CART_P01]. We therefore compared both platforms on the same aspirate pulls across a wide burden range.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Specimens came from 284 patients enrolled on two consecutive cooperative group protocols, with central processing within 24 hours. The flow panel used a harmonized 10-color configuration with a target acquisition of 4 million events and a stated limit of detection of 0.0005 percent. Sequencing required an index specimen with an identifiable dominant rearrangement, available in 271 of 284 patients, and reported burden per million nucleated cells. Hemodilution was estimated from mast cell and nucleated erythroid precursor content relative to a first-pull reference. Agreement was summarized by Cohen kappa overall and by burden decade. A Bayesian two-test latent class model with weakly informative priors estimated assay-specific sensitivity and specificity as a function of burden, cellularity, and prior therapy, assessed by posterior predictive checks.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Agreement was 99 percent above 0.1 percent burden, 84 percent between 0.001 and 0.01 percent, and 96 percent among specimens negative by both. Sequencing identified disease in 68 flow-negative specimens; of these, 41 percent came from pulls with mast cell content indicating dilution above the reference threshold. Nine specimens were flow-positive and sequencing-negative, six of which lacked a fully informative index rearrangement. Latent class estimates of sensitivity in the discordant range were 0.93 for sequencing and 0.71 for flow, converging above 0.01 percent. Five-year event-free survival was 84 percent for double-negative, 61 percent for sequencing-positive only, and 38 percent for double-positive patients (log-rank P less than 0.001). Adding sequencing status to a model containing flow status improved the concordance index from 0.66 to 0.72.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: The two platforms are not interchangeable in the burden range where treatment decisions are actually made, and the difference is prognostically meaningful rather than merely analytic: patients positive by sequencing alone had intermediate outcomes, which would be missed entirely by a phenotypic assay. Dilution explains a large share of the discrepancy and is correctable at the bedside by using first-pull material. Our results also caution against applying gating strategies developed before targeted immunotherapy to specimens obtained afterward, since blasts may no longer display the surface molecules used to identify them, a pattern documented in paired relapse material [PAPER:HEME_CART_P01]. Conversion rules derived here should be validated in myeloma, where plasma cell dilution behaves differently and where the informative index specimen is more often unavailable.

title: Undetectable Measurable Residual Disease as a Trial-Level Surrogate for Progression-Free Survival in Multiple Myeloma: A Meta-Analysis of 14 Randomized Trials

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We assembled individual patient data from 14 randomized trials enrolling 8236 patients with newly diagnosed or relapsed multiple myeloma in which measurable residual disease was assessed at a threshold of 10^-5 or deeper. At the patient level, undetectable disease at 12 months was associated with progression-free survival (hazard ratio 0.36, 95 percent confidence interval 0.31 to 0.42) consistently across subgroups defined by cytogenetic risk, transplant eligibility, and line of therapy. At the trial level, the association between treatment effects on the odds of undetectable disease and treatment effects on progression-free survival gave an R-squared of 0.72 (95 percent confidence interval 0.48 to 0.87), with a surrogate threshold effect corresponding to an odds ratio of 1.9. Association was stronger for sequencing-based assessment than for flow-based assessment, though confidence intervals overlapped.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Trials in this disease increasingly report depth of response as a primary or co-primary endpoint because progression-free survival now requires 5 or more years of follow-up in frontline settings. Regulatory acceptance of a response depth endpoint requires evidence at the trial level, not merely a prognostic association within arms, and it requires that assays be comparable across studies. A paired-assay analysis in acute lymphoblastic leukemia found that agreement between phenotypic and genomic platforms deteriorates precisely in the burden range where decisions are made, and that patients positive by sequencing alone occupy an intermediate prognostic category [PAPER:HEME_CART_P11]. Genomic assessment has accordingly been adopted as the primary depth endpoint in recent cellular therapy studies [PAPER:HEME_CART_P02]. We estimated both patient-level and trial-level surrogacy across the available randomized evidence.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Trials were eligible if randomized, enrolling at least 100 patients, and reporting disease assessment at 10^-5 or deeper in at least 70 percent of responders. Individual patient data were obtained for 14 of 19 eligible trials. Patient-level association was estimated by Cox models with undetectable status at 12 months as a landmark exposure, stratified by trial. Trial-level surrogacy used a two-stage weighted linear regression of log hazard ratios for progression-free survival on log odds ratios for undetectable disease, weighted by inverse variance, with leave-one-trial-out cross-validation and bootstrap confidence intervals. Prespecified sensitivity analyses examined assay platform, threshold depth, and inclusion of maintenance therapy. Heterogeneity was assessed by I-squared and by influence diagnostics on the trial-level regression.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median follow-up across trials was 54 months. Undetectable disease at 12 months was achieved by 2914 of 8236 patients. The patient-level hazard ratio was 0.36, with no evidence of effect modification by high-risk cytogenetics (interaction P equals 0.31) or transplant eligibility (P equals 0.44). Trial-level R-squared was 0.72 with a slope of 0.61, and leave-one-out estimates ranged from 0.66 to 0.78. Restricting to the 9 trials using sequencing-based assessment gave R-squared 0.78 versus 0.64 for the 5 using flow-based assessment. Depth mattered: assessment at 10^-6 gave a patient-level hazard ratio of 0.28 versus 0.41 at 10^-5. Two trials with large discordance between endpoints both tested agents with prolonged maintenance, in which progression-free benefit accrued after the landmark.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: The trial-level association supports use of depth of response as a surrogate in this disease at thresholds of 10^-5 and deeper, with the caveat that R-squared of 0.72 leaves meaningful uncertainty and that maintenance-heavy designs are the identifiable exception. The stronger association for genomic assessment is consistent with the analytic superiority of that platform near the detection floor demonstrated in paired comparison [PAPER:HEME_CART_P11], although platform was not randomized and reflects era and trial design. Our findings imply that assay and threshold should be prespecified and reported, since pooling across platforms attenuates the surrogate relationship. Extension to T-cell redirecting therapy is not yet possible, since few randomized trials of those agents have mature progression-free survival data.

title: Dominant-Negative TGFBR2 Armoring Restores Function of Mesothelin-Directed CAR T Cells in Orthotopic Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Mesothelin-directed CAR T cells kill pancreatic tumor lines efficiently in vitro yet fail against orthotopic tumors with intact desmoplastic stroma. We introduced a dominant-negative TGFBR2 into mesothelin-directed products and evaluated them in orthotopic KPC-derived organoid implants. Armored cells accumulated within viable tumor at a median of 184 cells per square millimeter at day 7 versus 41 for unarmored controls, produced 3.6-fold more interferon gamma after recovery from tissue, and extended median survival from 31 to 58 days. Cells recovered from tumor at day 14 showed reduced accessibility gains at PDCD1 and ENTPD1 relative to controls and retained a higher spare respiratory capacity. Armoring did not increase off-tumor injury to peritoneum or pleura on histologic review, and no weight loss exceeding 10 percent was observed.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Response rates for engineered T cells in epithelial cancers remain below 10 percent despite receptor architectures identical to those that produce durable remission in B-cell malignancy. The obstacles are properties of the tissue rather than of the receptor: a dense stroma, an absent adhesion program on tumor vessels, low oxygen tension, and abundant suppressive ligands, of which TGF-beta is the most consistently implicated. Dysfunction in these settings follows a stereotyped program with TOX at its center, and that program becomes fixed within weeks of transfer [PAPER:HEME_CART_P04]. Receptor architecture sets the rate at which cells traverse toward the terminal state under repeated engagement [PAPER:HEME_CART_P15]. We asked whether interrupting a single dominant suppressive input is sufficient to change that trajectory in tissue, or whether the barriers must be addressed jointly.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Mesothelin-directed receptors with 4-1BB endodomains were expressed in cells from three healthy donors, with or without a dominant-negative TGFBR2 co-expressed from the same vector. KPC-derived organoids were implanted into the pancreas of NSG mice, 12 animals per arm, with tumor followed by bioluminescence twice weekly. Engineered cells were given intravenously at 5e6 on day 10. At days 7 and 14 after transfer, tumors were harvested for multiplex imaging with cell segmentation, reported as engineered cells per square millimeter of viable tumor, and for recovery of engineered cells by sorting. Recovered cells were assayed for cytokine output, for transposase-accessible chromatin, and for spare respiratory capacity by extracellular flux. Comparisons used mixed models with donor as a random effect.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Armored cells reached 184 cells per square millimeter of viable tumor at day 7 versus 41 for controls (P less than 0.001), a difference that persisted at day 14. Interferon gamma production after ex vivo restimulation was 3.6-fold higher, and tumor necrosis factor double producers were 2.9-fold more frequent. Median survival extended from 31 to 58 days, with 4 of 12 armored animals tumor free at day 90. Chromatin profiling of recovered cells at day 14 showed 1840 regions with reduced accessibility gain relative to controls, enriched for regions near PDCD1, ENTPD1, and TOX. Spare respiratory capacity was 62 versus 28 picomoles per minute. Circulating engineered cells were detectable at day 30 in 9 of 12 armored versus 3 of 12 control animals.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Interrupting a single suppressive input produced a large functional gain in tissue, which argues that TGF-beta signaling is rate-limiting in this histology rather than one of many equally weighted barriers. The chromatin data indicate that armoring slows entry into the terminal program rather than reversing it once established, consistent with the commitment window described after infusion in patients [PAPER:HEME_CART_P04]. Two caveats bound the interpretation. First, orthotopic implants in immunodeficient animals lack an intact suppressive leukocyte compartment, so the contribution of host-derived suppression is underestimated. Second, accumulation within tumor improved but remained far below what is seen in marrow disease, implying that entry itself is a separate and unsolved problem requiring its own engineering solution.

title: CXCR2 Transduction and a Hypoxia-Responsive Cassette Improve Entry and Local Function of CAR T Cells in Ovarian Carcinoma Models

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Engineered T cells express predominantly CXCR3 while epithelial tumors secrete mainly CXCL1 and CXCL8, a receptor-ligand mismatch that limits entry. We transduced MUC16-directed products with CXCR2 and placed an interleukin 12 payload under a hypoxia-responsive promoter. In patient-derived intraperitoneal ovarian implants, CXCR2-modified cells reached a median 212 engineered cells per square millimeter of viable tumor at day 7 versus 58 for unmodified controls. Adding the hypoxia-restricted payload raised local interferon gamma 4.1-fold without detectable systemic interleukin 12, and combined modification extended median survival from 39 to 77 days. Intravital imaging showed that the improvement occurred at the step of extravasation rather than adhesion. Cells recovered at day 14 retained polyfunctionality, with double-producing fractions of 34 percent versus 12 percent in controls, and showed lower TOX transcript levels.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Armoring against a dominant suppressive ligand improves function once engineered cells are inside a tumor, but does not solve entry: a study of dominant-negative TGFBR2 in orthotopic pancreatic implants found a fourfold gain in intratumoral density yet absolute numbers far below those seen in marrow disease, and concluded that entry is a separable unsolved problem [PAPER:HEME_CART_P13]. Entry depends on matching the receptor repertoire of the transferred cells to the ligands the tumor actually produces. Because dysfunction accumulates rapidly once cells are in tissue and becomes epigenetically fixed [PAPER:HEME_CART_P04], accelerating entry may also preserve function by shortening the time spent in a suppressive environment. We tested receptor matching alone, local payload delivery alone, and both together in a factorial design.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: MUC16-directed receptors with 4-1BB endodomains were expressed with or without CXCR2 and with or without an interleukin 12 cassette driven by six hypoxia-response elements. Products were made from three healthy donors. Patient-derived ovarian implants were established intraperitoneally in NSG mice, 12 animals per arm across four arms. Engineered cells were given intravenously at 5e6. Intratumoral density was quantified by multiplex imaging with segmentation. Intravital imaging of photoconvertible reporter cells was used to distinguish rolling, adhesion, and extravasation events across 40 imaging fields. Systemic and intratumoral interleukin 12 were measured by immunoassay. Recovered cells were assessed for cytokine output and transcript levels. Analyses used mixed models with donor as a random effect and Holm correction across six planned contrasts.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Tumor lysates contained CXCL1 and CXCL8 at 18 and 24-fold the concentration of CXCL9 and CXCL10, while unmodified products expressed CXCR3 on 71 percent and CXCR2 on 4 percent of cells. CXCR2 transduction raised intratumoral density from 58 to 212 cells per square millimeter (P less than 0.001). Intravital imaging attributed the gain to extravasation events, which rose 3.8-fold, with no change in rolling or firm adhesion. The hypoxia-restricted payload raised intratumoral interferon gamma 4.1-fold with systemic interleukin 12 below the limit of quantification in 22 of 24 animals. Combined modification extended median survival from 39 to 77 days, with an interaction term indicating additive rather than synergistic effects. Granulocytic suppressor populations recruited by the same ligands increased 1.6-fold in treated tumors.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Matching receptor to available ligand improves entry substantially, and the intravital data localize the effect to a specific step, which prior density measurements could not do. A trade-off is evident: the same ligands recruit suppressive granulocytic populations, so receptor matching imports both the intended cells and their antagonists. Payload restriction to hypoxic regions solved the systemic toxicity that has limited constitutive cytokine armoring, and the absence of measurable circulating cytokine supports the design. Because the two modifications were additive rather than synergistic, the barriers appear to act in series, consistent with the conclusion drawn from single-barrier armoring in pancreatic models [PAPER:HEME_CART_P13]. Translation will require a construct in which both modifications fit within packaging limits, which currently forces compromises in binder affinity.

title: A Graded Receptor Series Shows That Early Signal Amplitude, Not Endodomain Identity, Sets Differentiation and Cytokine Output of CD19-Directed CAR T Cells

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: The contrast between CD28 and 4-1BB endodomains is usually described as a fixed property of the two modules. We built 16 CD19-directed receptors sharing the FMC63 binder and varying immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motif number, hinge length, and endodomain identity, and expressed them at matched vector copy number in cells from six donors. Early signal amplitude, summarized as area under the phospho-CD3 zeta curve over 60 minutes, spanned an eightfold range and predicted the rate of loss of the CD45RA-positive CCR7-positive fraction under repeated stimulation (R-squared 0.81). Two constructs with a single activation motif and a CD28 endodomain matched the CD28 reference for tumor control in NSG mice bearing NALM-6 while producing 54 percent lower peak human interleukin 6. Circulating engineered cells for these constructs were detectable at day 42 in 8 of 10 animals.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Products carrying CD28 expand faster and to higher peaks and are associated with more severe systemic inflammation, while those carrying 4-1BB signal more slowly and remain detectable far longer. Because the two modules are compared as intact units, endodomain identity and signal strength are confounded, and it is not known which of the two determines the observed differences. Product composition at release is itself associated with outcome, with an early-differentiation CD8 population enriched in patients with durable remission [PAPER:HEME_CART_P03], and the transcriptional program that terminates function is governed by TOX and becomes fixed within weeks [PAPER:HEME_CART_P04]. If signal amplitude rather than module identity sets the rate of that trajectory, then constructs could be tuned continuously rather than chosen from two options.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: All 16 receptors shared the FMC63 binder and a common lentiviral backbone, with vector copy number verified by droplet digital PCR and matched to within 20 percent. Cells from six healthy donors were used for every assay. Phospho-flow for CD3 zeta, ERK, and AKT was performed at 2, 10, and 60 minutes after engagement with fixed-density antigen-coated beads. Repeat stimulation used irradiated NALM-6 added every 3 days for five rounds, with counts, surface phenotype, and cytokine output at each round. In vivo, 10 mice per construct received 1e6 cells with tumor followed by bioluminescence and engineered cells quantified in 50 microliters of blood twice weekly. Human interleukin 6 and interferon gamma were measured at days 3, 5, and 7. Hierarchical models included donor-level random intercepts.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Area under the phospho-CD3 zeta curve varied eightfold across constructs and correlated with the per-round decline in the CD45RA-positive CCR7-positive fraction (R-squared 0.81) and with cumulative expansion across five rounds (R-squared 0.74). Endodomain identity added no explanatory power once amplitude was included in the model (likelihood ratio P equals 0.28). Two single-motif CD28 constructs achieved tumor control indistinguishable from the three-motif CD28 reference (median survival 64 versus 61 days) with peak human interleukin 6 of 96 versus 209 picograms per milliliter. Engineered cells for these constructs were detectable at day 42 in 8 of 10 animals versus 2 of 10 for the reference. Chromatin profiling of cells after four stimulation rounds showed that accessibility gains near PDCD1 scaled monotonically with amplitude.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Signal amplitude, not module identity, explains the classical contrast between the two endodomains, and amplitude can be tuned by changing motif number without changing the module. The practical consequence is a design rule: a construct can be selected before manufacture using a 60-minute in vitro assay that predicts both differentiation rate and inflammatory output. Our results provide a mechanistic account for the compositional association between an early-differentiation population and durable remission [PAPER:HEME_CART_P03], since lower-amplitude constructs preserve that population through repeated engagement. The extent to which these findings extend beyond B-lineage targets is unclear, because antigen density and engagement frequency differ substantially in epithelial tumors, where sustained low-level engagement may favor different amplitude settings.

title: Axicabtagene Ciloleucel versus Tisagenlecleucel for Relapsed Large B-Cell Lymphoma: Effectiveness and Toxicity in 1284 Registry Patients

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We analyzed 1284 adults infused commercially for relapsed large B-cell lymphoma between 2018 and 2020, of whom 742 received axicabtagene ciloleucel and 542 tisagenlecleucel. After stabilized inverse probability weighting on 18 baseline covariates, 12-month progression-free survival was 44 percent versus 33 percent (hazard ratio 0.78, 95 percent confidence interval 0.66 to 0.92) and 12-month overall survival 61 versus 54 percent. Grade 3 or higher cytokine release syndrome occurred in 8 versus 3 percent and grade 3 or higher neurotoxicity in 24 versus 6 percent. Intensive care admission was 21 versus 8 percent and 100-day non-relapse mortality 4.4 versus 2.6 percent. Fifty-eight percent of the cohort would not have met pivotal trial eligibility. Median interval from collection to infusion was 28 days, during which 9 percent of intended recipients progressed and never received treatment.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Pivotal trials of the two commercial products enrolled fitter patients closer to academic centers and were never compared head to head. Because the two products differ in signaling architecture, expansion kinetics, and toxicity profile, clinicians must choose between them using indirect evidence. Serial sampling studies have shown that severe neurologic events follow a distinct upstream pathway from hemodynamic toxicity and are more frequent with the faster-expanding product [PAPER:HEME_CART_P07]. Mechanistic work has attributed those kinetic differences to early signal amplitude rather than to the identity of the signaling module [PAPER:HEME_CART_P15]. Whether the resulting differences translate into an effectiveness difference outside trial populations, and at what cost in toxicity and resource use, is the question addressed here.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients were identified in a national cellular therapy registry with mandatory reporting and 12-month follow-up. Eighteen baseline covariates were used to construct stabilized inverse probability of treatment weights, with balance assessed by standardized mean differences below 0.1. Weighted Kaplan-Meier estimates and weighted Cox models were reported with robust variance and center-level clustering. Trial eligibility was reconstructed from published protocols and applied retrospectively. The interval from collection to infusion was analyzed with a cloning and censoring approach to remove immortal time. Toxicity was graded by ASTCT criteria as reported by centers, with 12 percent of records audited for concordance. Sensitivity analyses used E-values to quantify the unmeasured confounding required to nullify the observed effectiveness difference.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Weighted 12-month progression-free survival was 44 versus 33 percent (hazard ratio 0.78) and the E-value for the point estimate was 1.87. Grade 3 or higher neurotoxicity was fourfold more common with the faster-expanding product, with median duration 5 days and intensive care admission in 21 percent. Bridging therapy was given to 63 percent, and high-intensity bridging was independently associated with inferior progression-free survival (hazard ratio 1.34). Median collection-to-infusion interval was 28 days, and 9 percent of intended recipients progressed before treatment. Annual center volume above 20 infusions was associated with lower 100-day non-relapse mortality (2.9 versus 5.8 percent). Patients with Medicaid coverage and those traveling more than 100 miles had longer intervals from referral to collection, by a median of 11 and 8 days respectively.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Effectiveness favored the faster-expanding product modestly, at the cost of substantially more neurologic toxicity and intensive care use, so the choice depends on local capacity as much as on biology. The toxicity gap is consistent with the pathway ordering established by serial sampling, in which higher early inflammatory amplitude drives endothelial injury and barrier failure [PAPER:HEME_CART_P07]. Because the underlying kinetic difference is attributable to signal amplitude, which is tunable [PAPER:HEME_CART_P15], future constructs may not force this trade-off. Two structural findings deserve attention: nearly a tenth of intended recipients never reached infusion, and patients with public insurance or long travel distances waited longer at every step. Effectiveness estimates that condition on infusion therefore describe a selected population.

title: Travel Distance, Insurance Type, and Race in the Referral Funnel for Commercial CAR T-Cell Therapy: A Linked Claims and Registry Analysis

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Linking a national cellular therapy registry to commercial and public claims, we estimated how many patients with label-eligible relapsed aggressive lymphoma were referred, collected, and infused across 306 hospital referral regions between 2019 and 2022. Of an estimated 14200 label-eligible patients, 41 percent were referred to a certified center, 27 percent underwent collection, and 22 percent were infused. Referral probability fell by 9 percent per 25 miles of driving distance and was lower for Medicaid enrollees (adjusted odds ratio 0.62) and for Black patients (0.71) after adjustment for age, comorbidity, and disease characteristics. Among those referred, the median interval from referral to infusion was 51 days, and 14 percent died or progressed beyond eligibility during that interval. Regions in the lowest quartile of certified center density had referral rates less than half those of the highest quartile.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Outcome analyses of cellular therapy describe patients who were infused, which cannot address who never arrived. Registry comparisons of the two commercial products for aggressive lymphoma showed that nearly a tenth of intended recipients progressed before infusion and that patients with public insurance or long travel distances waited longer at every step [PAPER:HEME_CART_P16]. Those observations were confined to patients already at a certified center. The larger loss almost certainly occurs earlier, at referral, where the decision is made by community oncologists who may see one candidate per year. Interventions that shorten the interval between collection and infusion, including banked donor-derived products that are available on demand, have been proposed partly on the grounds that they would reduce this attrition [PAPER:HEME_CART_P09].

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Label-eligible patients were identified from claims by diagnosis, treatment sequence, and absence of exclusionary conditions, using an algorithm with positive predictive value of 0.86 validated against 400 chart-abstracted cases. Registry records were linked by a deterministic-probabilistic hybrid with an 89 percent match rate. Driving distance was computed from the patient residence centroid to the nearest certified center. Multilevel logistic models estimated referral, collection, and infusion probabilities with random intercepts for hospital referral region, adjusting for age, comorbidity index, lines of therapy, disease bulk, and area deprivation index. Small-area estimates were smoothed with spatial random effects. Interval analyses used competing-risk models with death and disease progression as competing events.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 14200 estimated label-eligible patients, 5822 were referred, 3834 collected, and 3124 infused. Each 25 miles of driving distance reduced the odds of referral by 9 percent (95 percent credible interval 6 to 12 percent). Adjusted odds of referral were 0.62 for Medicaid enrollees and 0.71 for Black patients, and 0.58 for patients in the highest quintile of area deprivation. Once referred, disparities narrowed markedly: adjusted odds of infusion given referral were 0.91 for Medicaid and 0.96 for Black patients, neither significant. Median referral-to-infusion interval was 51 days, of which 28 days fell between collection and infusion; 14 percent of referred patients died or progressed beyond eligibility. Referral rates in the lowest quartile of center density were 26 percent versus 57 percent in the highest.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Attrition in this pathway is dominated by referral rather than by what happens after a patient reaches a certified center, and the gradients we observe by insurance, race, and distance largely disappear once referral occurs. That pattern points toward interventions aimed at community oncologists and at regional capacity rather than at center-level processes. The 51-day interval from referral to infusion is itself a major source of loss, and roughly half of it precedes collection, which means that shortening the collection-to-infusion interval alone, as banked donor-derived products would do [PAPER:HEME_CART_P09], addresses only part of the problem. Claims-based eligibility estimation is the principal limitation, since disease bulk and performance status are imperfectly captured and could bias the denominator upward.

title: Severe Infection Density and Immunoglobulin Replacement during Continuous Teclistamab Therapy in Relapsed Myeloma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Among 212 patients receiving teclistamab for relapsed multiple myeloma across six centers, grade 3 or higher infections occurred at 1.24 events per patient-year during the first 12 months, with a peak between months 2 and 5. Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia occurred in 9 patients, cytomegalovirus reactivation requiring therapy in 17, and invasive mold infection in 6. Median immunoglobulin G nadir was 302 milligrams per deciliter, and 141 patients received replacement. In an Andersen-Gill model, cumulative corticosteroid dose for cytokine release syndrome above 100 milligrams dexamethasone equivalent (rate ratio 1.68), immunoglobulin G below 400 milligrams per deciliter (1.54), and neutropenia beyond 14 days (1.47) were independently associated with infection density. Replacement initiated before the second cycle was associated with a rate ratio of 0.63 in a landmark analysis. Infection accounted for 21 of 38 non-relapse deaths.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Unlike a single cellular infusion, bispecific antibodies are administered continuously until progression, so the immunodeficiency they cause does not resolve. Resistance analyses in this setting have shown that most failures occur with the target intact and with accumulating effector dysfunction rather than antigen loss [PAPER:HEME_CART_P05], which means patients remain on therapy for long intervals and accumulate exposure. Comparative experience with a target that spares normal plasma cells reported lower severe infection rates, at 24 percent over 12 months, suggesting that on-target plasma cell depletion is a major contributor rather than an incidental one [PAPER:HEME_CART_P06]. Prolonged cytopenia is a second contributor and is increasingly recognized as marrow-intrinsic in heavily pretreated patients [PAPER:HEME_CART_P21]. We characterized infection as a recurrent process with time-varying exposure.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Two hundred twelve consecutive patients starting teclistamab between 2022 and 2024 at six centers were followed for 12 months or until death. Infections were graded by CTCAE version 5 and adjudicated centrally by two infectious disease physicians blinded to center, with a third resolving disagreements. Immunoglobulin G, absolute neutrophil count, and lymphocyte subsets were recorded at baseline and monthly. Cumulative corticosteroid exposure was computed as dexamethasone equivalents. Recurrent-event analysis used Andersen-Gill models with robust variance and center-level frailty, with corticosteroid dose and immunoglobulin level as time-varying covariates. The effect of early replacement was estimated in a 60-day landmark analysis with inverse probability weighting for treatment initiation. Prophylaxis practices differed by center and were included as fixed effects.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Severe infection density was 1.24 events per patient-year overall and 2.10 during months 2 through 5. Respiratory viral infections were most frequent (86 events), followed by bacterial pneumonia (61) and bacteremia (37). Median immunoglobulin G nadir was 302 milligrams per deciliter at a median of 10 weeks; 141 patients received replacement, initiated before cycle 2 in 58. Rate ratios were 1.68 for cumulative corticosteroid dose above 100 milligrams, 1.54 for immunoglobulin G below 400, and 1.47 for neutropenia beyond 14 days. Early replacement was associated with a rate ratio of 0.63 (95 percent confidence interval 0.44 to 0.90). Twenty-one of 38 non-relapse deaths were infectious. Patients treated at centers requiring inpatient step-up dosing had similar infection density but 6 additional hospital days per patient-year.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Infection density in this cohort exceeded what is reported after a single cellular infusion by roughly twofold and peaked in the third to fifth month, later than clinicians commonly anticipate. The association with cumulative corticosteroid exposure is actionable, since much of that exposure is given for hemodynamic toxicity that alternative agents can control. The lower severe infection rate reported for a target that spares normal plasma cells [PAPER:HEME_CART_P06] supports on-target humoral depletion as a principal mechanism rather than a secondary one, and argues for early rather than threshold-triggered replacement, a question now under randomized evaluation. Requirements for inpatient step-up dosing add hospital days without measurable safety benefit and remain a practical obstacle to delivering these agents outside large centers.

title: Multisite Analytical Validation of a Standardized Ten-Color Next-Generation Flow Assay: Limit of Detection, Reproducibility, and Sample Adequacy

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We validated a harmonized 10-color flow cytometric assay across 11 laboratories using 480 spiked and clinical specimens. With acquisition of 4 million events, the limit of detection was 0.0007 percent and the lower limit of quantification 0.002 percent, both meeting prespecified acceptance criteria. Inter-laboratory coefficients of variation were 14 percent above 0.01 percent burden and 38 percent between 0.002 and 0.01 percent. Concordance with immunoglobulin clonotype sequencing on 264 paired clinical specimens was 89 percent, with discordance concentrated below 0.01 percent, matching earlier single-center estimates. Sample adequacy was the dominant failure mode: 17 percent of specimens contained fewer than 2 million viable events, and hemodilution assessed by mast cell content exceeded the acceptance threshold in 23 percent. Assay performance did not differ between plasma cell and B-lymphoblast configurations, but median processing delay above 36 hours degraded viability sufficiently to raise the detection limit fourfold.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Phenotypic detection of low-burden disease is used to guide consolidation, to define response depth in registration studies, and increasingly to trigger intervention in the absence of clinical relapse. Its analytic performance is nevertheless reported inconsistently, and multisite reproducibility near the detection floor has rarely been measured. A paired comparison in lymphoblastic leukemia found that phenotypic and genomic platforms agree well above 0.1 percent but diverge substantially between 0.001 and 0.01 percent, with dilution of the aspirate explaining a large share of phenotypic false negatives [PAPER:HEME_CART_P11]. Because trial-level evidence supporting response depth as a decision endpoint rests on pooled results from both platforms [PAPER:HEME_CART_P12], the analytic properties of each must be characterized before results are combined. This study reports a formal validation across laboratories.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Eleven laboratories received identical reagent lots, a common instrument setup protocol with standardized photomultiplier voltages, and a shared gating template. Spiked panels were prepared by diluting characterized cell lines into normal marrow at nominal burdens from 0.0005 to 1 percent, with 10 replicates per level. Clinical specimens comprised 264 aspirates with paired immunoglobulin clonotype sequencing. Limit of detection was defined as the lowest level at which 95 percent of replicates yielded at least 20 clustered events; lower limit of quantification required a coefficient of variation below 25 percent. Hemodilution was quantified from mast cell and nucleated erythroid precursor content. Mixed-effects models with laboratory as a random effect estimated variance components. Processing delay was analyzed as a continuous covariate.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Across 11 laboratories the pooled limit of detection was 0.0007 percent and the lower limit of quantification 0.002 percent. Laboratory contributed 19 percent of total variance at burdens above 0.01 percent and 44 percent below it. Concordance with the genomic platform was 89 percent overall, 98 percent above 0.1 percent, and 79 percent between 0.001 and 0.01 percent, with the genomic assay positive in 31 of 38 discordant pairs. Seventeen percent of clinical specimens fell below the 2 million event threshold, and 23 percent exceeded the hemodilution limit; excluding inadequate specimens raised concordance to 94 percent. Processing beyond 36 hours reduced viability from a median 91 to 68 percent and raised the effective detection limit from 0.0007 to 0.003 percent. Gating of specimens obtained after therapy directed at lineage surface molecules required template modification in 22 cases.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: The assay meets its analytic specification when specimen quality is adequate, and most observed disagreement with the genomic platform is attributable to preanalytic factors rather than to the measurement itself. That distinction matters because preanalytic failures are correctable at the bedside by using first-pull material and by shortening transport, whereas analytic limits are not. Our concordance profile reproduces the burden-dependent pattern described in a paired single-center comparison [PAPER:HEME_CART_P11], with the added observation that between-laboratory variance more than doubles below 0.01 percent. Laboratories reporting results in this range should state both the number of events acquired and a dilution assessment. Templates developed before the introduction of therapies directed at lineage surface molecules required modification for a subset of post-treatment specimens, since the markers used for identification may no longer be displayed.

title: Base-Edited CD33-Negative Hematopoietic Grafts Permit Sustained CD33-Directed CAR T-Cell Pressure in Models of Acute Myeloid Leukemia

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Every candidate surface target in acute myeloid leukemia is shared with normal hematopoietic progenitors, so effective redirected cytotoxicity produces prolonged marrow aplasia. We used an adenine base editor delivered as messenger RNA with a chemically modified guide to change a single codon in CD33 exon 2, abolishing binder recognition while preserving protein expression and sialic acid binding. Editing reached 89 percent in mobilized CD34-positive cells from 10 donors, with colony-forming output and lineage distribution unchanged. Mice reconstituted with edited progenitors showed normal multilineage output at 20 weeks. Challenge with CD33-directed CAR T cells cleared primary leukemia grafts in 9 of 12 animals while edited human myeloid cells were preserved at 71 percent of pre-challenge levels, versus 6 percent in unedited controls. Marrow burden fell below 0.01 percent in 8 of 12 animals and surviving blasts showed reduced surface target density.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Redirected cellular therapy has transformed outcomes in B-lineage disease but has produced no approved product in myeloid leukemia, because the targets are shared with the compartment that must survive. Affinity tuning cannot separate identical molecules, so the therapeutic window must be created elsewhere. Editing the graft rather than the receptor inverts the problem. Clinical experience with multiplex-edited donor-derived CAR products has established that ribonucleoprotein-based editing of primary human cells is feasible at scale and can meet release specifications [PAPER:HEME_CART_P09]. Paired specimen studies in lymphoblastic leukemia have also shown that sustained single-target pressure selects for reduced surface density and outright loss [PAPER:HEME_CART_P01], which makes the durability of pressure, and therefore the survival of the healthy compartment, a central design question.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Mobilized CD34-positive cells from 10 healthy donors were electroporated with base editor messenger RNA and a guide targeting the codon encoding the recognized residue in CD33 exon 2. Editing was quantified by amplicon sequencing; surface protein was measured with antibody-binding capacity beads using two non-overlapping antibodies. Off-target activity was assessed by orthogonal genome-wide capture and by transcriptome-wide analysis of adenosine deamination. NSG-SGM3 mice received 2e5 edited or unedited progenitors and were followed 20 weeks. Primary leukemia grafts from 12 patients were established and challenged with 5e6 CD33-directed CAR T cells carrying 4-1BB endodomains. Surviving blasts were recovered at day 28 for target density measurement. Comparisons used mixed models with donor and patient as random effects and Holm adjustment.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median editing was 89 percent with no detectable indels at the target site and no verified off-target edits among the top 40 candidate loci. Colony-forming unit output was 104 percent of unedited controls, and erythroid, myeloid, and megakaryocytic distributions were unchanged. Human chimerism at 20 weeks was 62 percent for edited and 58 percent for unedited grafts. After challenge, human myeloid cells derived from edited grafts were preserved at 71 percent of pre-challenge levels versus 6 percent for unedited grafts (P less than 0.001), while leukemia burden fell below 0.01 percent in 8 of 12 animals. Among the 4 animals with persistent disease, surviving blasts showed a median 2900 target molecules per cell versus 8400 at baseline. No increase in graft-versus-host disease was observed in the reconstituted animals.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Shielding the healthy compartment by a single-codon change preserves protein function while removing recognition, which is essential for receptors that participate in normal signaling and would be compromised by nuclease-mediated disruption. Preservation of edited myeloid output under sustained pressure is the key result, since it converts a therapy that cannot be given for more than days into one that can be maintained. Selection of blasts with reduced surface density among the animals with persistent disease mirrors the density-dependent escape described after sustained pressure in lymphoblastic leukemia [PAPER:HEME_CART_P01] and argues for dual targeting or for a second shielded epitope. Translation requires a clinical path in which edited progenitors are transplanted before redirected therapy, which is feasible only for patients who are transplant candidates.

title: Pre-Infusion Clonal Hematopoiesis, Not Inflammatory Intensity, Explains Prolonged Cytopenia after CAR T-Cell Therapy

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We sequenced marrow collected before fludarabine and cyclophosphamide conditioning in 388 consecutive adults treated with commercial products for aggressive lymphoma at eight centers. Clonal hematopoiesis at a variant allele fraction of at least 2 percent was present in 39 percent, most commonly involving DNMT3A, PPM1D, and TET2. Neutrophil counts remained below 500 per microliter beyond day 30 in 96 patients. PPM1D and TP53 variants were associated with prolonged cytopenia (adjusted odds ratio 2.7 and 3.1), whereas DNMT3A variants were not. Peak ferritin, C-reactive protein, and interleukin 6 were associated with cytopenia in unadjusted analysis but explained only 11 percent of the effect in formal mediation analysis, with the remainder attributable to the marrow-intrinsic path. Patients with prolonged cytopenia had more infections and more readmissions but similar progression-free survival.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Roughly a quarter of patients have profound neutropenia beyond the first month after infusion, and management is empirical. Two mechanisms are usually invoked and rarely separated: an intrinsically damaged marrow in a heavily pretreated population, and sustained inflammation from the infusion itself. Registry comparisons have shown that non-relapse mortality after infusion is concentrated in the first 100 days and is driven largely by infection in cytopenic patients [PAPER:HEME_CART_P16]. Serial sampling has characterized the inflammatory trajectory in detail, including its dependence on monocyte-derived interleukin 1 beta and subsequent endothelial injury [PAPER:HEME_CART_P07], and a prophylaxis study showed that this trajectory can be blunted substantially without loss of efficacy [PAPER:HEME_CART_P08]. If inflammation were the dominant cause of cytopenia, that intervention should have shortened it.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Three hundred eighty-eight consecutive adults treated between 2019 and 2022 at eight centers had marrow aspirated before conditioning chemotherapy. Error-corrected sequencing of 61 genes used unique molecular identifiers with a variant allele fraction floor of 0.5 percent; variants were reported at a 2 percent threshold for the primary analysis. Prolonged cytopenia was defined as an absolute neutrophil count below 500 per microliter beyond day 30. Logistic models adjusted for age, prior lines, prior autologous transplant, baseline counts, and disease burden. Mediation used the natural effects framework with peak ferritin, C-reactive protein, and interleukin 6 area under the curve as candidate mediators, with 2000 bootstrap replicates. Infections and readmissions were abstracted centrally. Progression-free survival was compared by Cox regression with center-level frailty.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Clonal hematopoiesis was present in 151 of 388 patients; DNMT3A accounted for 61 variants, PPM1D 44, and TET2 38. Ninety-six patients had prolonged cytopenia. Adjusted odds ratios were 2.7 for PPM1D, 3.1 for TP53, 1.1 for DNMT3A, and 1.4 for TET2. Prior autologous transplant (odds ratio 2.2) and more than three prior lines (1.9) were independently associated. Peak ferritin above 5000 nanograms per milliliter was associated with cytopenia in unadjusted models, but mediation analysis attributed only 11 percent of the total effect to the inflammatory path (95 percent confidence interval 3 to 22 percent). Patients with prolonged cytopenia had 1.9 times more grade 3 infections and 2.3 times more 100-day readmissions, with 12-month progression-free survival of 41 versus 45 percent (P equals 0.38).

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Prolonged cytopenia in this cohort was principally a property of the marrow the patient brought to treatment, not of the inflammatory response the treatment produced. The variant-class specificity supports that reading, since PPM1D and TP53 variants mark prior genotoxic selection while DNMT3A variants, which are the most common overall, carried no excess risk. The practical implication is that anti-inflammatory strategies effective against neurologic toxicity [PAPER:HEME_CART_P08] should not be expected to shorten cytopenia, and that patients with high-risk variants should be identified before infusion and considered for planned stem cell boost. Because non-relapse mortality is concentrated in cytopenic patients during the first 100 days [PAPER:HEME_CART_P16], pre-infusion sequencing may be more useful for supportive care planning than for treatment selection.

title: Vector Integration Sites and Clonal Origin of T-Cell Neoplasms Arising after CD19-Directed CAR T-Cell Therapy in 1932 Patients

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Among 1932 adults treated with commercial CD19-directed products at eight centers with a median follow-up of 46 months, 7 developed a T-cell neoplasm, giving a 4-year cumulative incidence of 0.42 percent with death and relapse as competing risks. Banked material was available for all 7. The transgene was detected in tumor cells in 3 cases; in 2 of these the integration was intronic in genes with no established role in lymphomagenesis, and in 1 the integration lay 14 kilobases upstream of a transcription factor with a modest increase in its expression. Four cases were transgene negative. Six of 7 patients carried clonal hematopoiesis before infusion and 5 had received prior autologous transplant. Myeloid neoplasms were more common than T-cell neoplasms, with a 4-year cumulative incidence of 3.1 percent.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Reports of T-cell neoplasms after infusion prompted regulatory action, but the published cases lacked denominators, systematic follow-up, and banked material, so causal attribution to the integrating vector could not be evaluated. The relevant background risk is substantial: patients reaching cellular therapy have typically received multiple genotoxic regimens, and pre-infusion sequencing shows clonal hematopoiesis in roughly 40 percent, with variant classes marking prior selection pressure associated with adverse hematologic outcomes [PAPER:HEME_CART_P21]. Registry analyses have established the expected rates of non-relapse events in this population [PAPER:HEME_CART_P16]. Long-term integration site monitoring was built into early trials of nuclease-edited donor-derived products for exactly this purpose [PAPER:HEME_CART_P09]. We report incidence with competing-risk methods and molecular characterization of every incident case.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: The cohort comprised 1932 consecutive adults treated between 2018 and 2023 with mandatory annual follow-up. Incident second cancers were confirmed by central pathology review. For T-cell neoplasms, transgene presence was assessed by droplet digital PCR on microdissected tumor and by targeted capture of the vector backbone; integration sites were recovered by ligation-mediated PCR with unique molecular identifiers and mapped to the reference genome. Clonality was assessed by T-cell receptor gene sequencing on tumor and on the original infusion product where available. Pre-infusion marrow sequencing used a 61-gene error-corrected panel. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated with death and disease relapse as competing risks, and comparisons with an age- and therapy-matched external cohort used standardized incidence ratios.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Seven T-cell neoplasms occurred at a median of 21 months (range 4 to 39), comprising 4 peripheral T-cell lymphomas, 2 T-cell large granular lymphocytic leukemias, and 1 hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma. Four-year cumulative incidence was 0.42 percent, and the standardized incidence ratio against the matched external cohort was 1.6 (95 percent confidence interval 0.7 to 3.3). Transgene was detected in 3 of 7 tumors; recovered integrations were intronic in NCOA2 and in an uncharacterized locus, and one lay 14 kilobases upstream of TCF12 with a 2.1-fold expression increase. In no case did the tumor clonotype match a dominant clonotype in the infusion product. Six of 7 patients had pre-infusion clonal hematopoiesis. Myeloid neoplasms occurred in 49 patients, 4-year cumulative incidence 3.1 percent.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: T-cell neoplasms after infusion are rare, occur at a rate not clearly above the background for this heavily pretreated population, and are transgene negative in the majority. Where the transgene was present, the integration sites were not obviously oncogenic and the tumor clonotypes did not match dominant clones in the transferred product, which argues against insertional transformation of an infused cell as the usual mechanism. The strong association with pre-infusion clonal hematopoiesis and prior autologous transplant points instead to a preexisting predisposed hematopoietic compartment, consistent with the marrow-intrinsic explanation established for prolonged cytopenia in this population [PAPER:HEME_CART_P21]. Myeloid neoplasms, which are sevenfold more common, deserve more attention than the events that prompted regulatory concern. Continued annual integration monitoring, as instituted for donor-derived edited products [PAPER:HEME_CART_P09], remains appropriate.

title: Keratopathy and Dose Modification with Belantamab Mafodotin in Relapsed Myeloma: Ophthalmologic Outcomes of an Extended Interval Schedule

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Belantamab mafodotin is an antibody-drug conjugate directed at BCMA and carrying a monomethyl auristatin F payload; its principal toxicity is a corneal microcyst-like epitheliopathy unrelated to plasma cell biology. In 158 patients with relapsed multiple myeloma randomized to 2.5 milligrams per kilogram every 3 weeks or every 9 weeks, grade 3 or higher keratopathy occurred in 44 versus 19 percent, and best corrected visual acuity declined by 2 or more lines in 33 versus 14 percent. Overall response was 34 versus 31 percent and median progression-free survival 4.8 versus 4.6 months. Depth of response at 10^-5 was reached by 9 patients overall. Dose delays for ocular findings occurred in 71 percent of the 3-week arm. Grade 3 or higher infection occurred in 11 percent, substantially below rates reported with T-cell redirecting agents against the same target.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Agents directed at BCMA now include cellular products, bispecific antibodies, and antibody-drug conjugates, which share a target but differ entirely in mechanism and toxicity. For the conjugate, activity depends on internalization and payload delivery rather than on effector recruitment, so effector dysfunction is irrelevant and the dominant toxicity is off-target corneal epithelial injury from payload uptake by limbal stem cells. Longitudinal resistance work on T-cell redirecting agents against this target has shown that most failures occur with the target intact and with accumulating effector dysfunction [PAPER:HEME_CART_P05], a mechanism with no counterpart here. Response depth measured at 10^-5 or deeper is the accepted comparator across these classes because of its trial-level association with progression-free survival [PAPER:HEME_CART_P12]. We report a randomized comparison of two dosing intervals.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: One hundred fifty-eight patients with relapsed multiple myeloma after at least four prior lines were randomized 1:1 to belantamab mafodotin 2.5 milligrams per kilogram every 3 weeks or every 9 weeks. Ophthalmologic examination including slit-lamp biomicroscopy and best corrected visual acuity was performed at baseline and before each dose, with grading by the Keratopathy and Visual Acuity scale by masked ophthalmologists. The primary endpoint was grade 3 or higher ocular findings. Response was assessed by International Myeloma Working Group criteria and depth of response by immunoglobulin clonotype sequencing at a floor of 10^-6 in patients achieving complete response. Infections were graded by CTCAE version 5. Time-to-event endpoints used Cox models stratified by cytogenetic risk and prior lines.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Grade 3 or higher keratopathy occurred in 35 of 79 patients on the 3-week schedule versus 15 of 79 on the 9-week schedule (P equals 0.001). Visual acuity declined by 2 or more lines in 26 versus 11 patients, and 4 patients in the 3-week arm reached 20/200 or worse in the better eye. Median time to first ocular event was 5.6 weeks. Dose delays occurred in 56 patients on the 3-week schedule. Overall response was 27 of 79 versus 25 of 79, and median progression-free survival 4.8 versus 4.6 months (hazard ratio 0.96). Nine patients reached undetectable disease at 10^-5, five of whom remained progression free beyond 18 months. Grade 3 or higher infection occurred in 17 patients overall, and no patient required immunoglobulin replacement for recurrent infection.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Extending the dosing interval halved severe ocular toxicity without measurable loss of activity, which supports a schedule change rather than dose reduction as the preferred mitigation. The dissociation between exposure and efficacy is expected for a conjugate whose antitumor effect depends on cumulative internalized payload while corneal injury tracks peak exposure to limbal cells. Infection rates were markedly lower than those reported for continuously administered T-cell redirecting agents against the same target, which is consistent with the absence of on-target depletion of normal plasma cells by an internalizing conjugate. Response depth was rarely achieved at this stage of disease, so the depth endpoint contributes little discrimination here despite its established trial-level behavior in earlier lines [PAPER:HEME_CART_P12].
